Europe's youth set to join mass cost of living protests in 25 countries
Youth protests are set to take place in more than 25 countries in Europe on Friday and over the weekend, coalition organisers said, as demostrators seek to increase pressure on governments over issues including soaring housing c
items.text:
Europe's youth set to join mass cost of living protests in 25 countries
Youth protests are set to take place in more than 25 countries in Europe on Friday and over the weekend, coalition organisers said, as demostrators seek to increase pressure on governments over issues including soaring housing costs and deteriorating learning conditions with a show of cross-border solidarity.
Protesters across Europe are set to take to the streets on Friday in a show of cross-border solidarity, joining coordinated demonstrations against the rising cost of living, militarisation and other causes, in a bid to increase pressure on their governments.
After weeks of protests in several European nations, unions and activists from France, Britain, Belgium, Spain, Italy, Portugal and Greece want to raise the stakes by holding simultaneous rallies on Friday and over the upcoming weekend.
While local grievances have fuelled the fire, the movements that have brought hundreds of thousands onto the streets are linked by shared continent-wide concerns, including soaring housing costs, deteriorating learning conditions, stagnant pay and increased military spending.
The demonstrations come as Russia's invasion of Ukraine approaches its fifth year and ahead of a series of key elections in Spain, France, Italy and Greece.
Read moreSpain’s general strike puts housing crisis at centre of upcoming elections
A youth-led coalition said young people in more than 25 countries were expected to join the protests.
"It's a really important event in giving a platform to the youth voice throughout the country and expressing our need for systemic and immediate change for our futures," said Zennor Tyndale-Biscoe, a 17-year-old student who planned to demonstrate in Truro in southwest England.
"We believe strongly in the youth voice and the effect it will have on an adult world," Tyndale-Biscoe said, also citing the French youth protests.
'Radical transformation'
The youth-led coalition urged a "radical transformation of the system we live in" and encouraged young people to protest against militarisation and social injustice.
"Fight for our future, not their wars!" said the coalition of more than 50 youth- and student-led groups.
Among the organisers are also France's Yellow Vests, a movement that rattled President Emmanuel Macron with street protests in 2018 and 2019.
Read more'No justice, no peace': Fifth round of protests sweep across France
The unions and housing rights activists put forward six broad demands ranging from a guaranteed right to housing for everyone to taxing the rich and ending rearmament policies.
While the European Union seeks to rearm in the face of the Russian threat, the protest organisers say funds allocated to rearmament should be spent on education, youth policies and housing.
In Germany, fears of a possible reintroduction of military service have led many young people to join the protests.
Read more'Gen Z' demonstrations across Germany demand more education funding
"While seemingly unlimited amounts of money are being poured into the military and the infrastructure supporting the military, the welfare state is being dismantled," said Hannes Kramer, a German student protester.
'Call for change'
While organisers say that hundreds of protests and strikes are expected to take place in countries including Portugal, Croatia and Switzerland, the scale of the mobilisation remains difficult to predict.
In France, the calls to protest coincide with the eighth anniversary of the Yellow Vest movement, which began as a campaign against rising fuel taxes before evolving into a broader protest over the cost of living.
In Italy, the demonstrations will coincide with a general strike set to affect transport, schools and hospitals, with the CGIL trade union dubbing the protests "the country's call for change".
In Spain, the protests fall on the anniversary of the death of dictator Francisco Franco, with youth demonstrations expected at midday and anti-fascist rallies planned for the evening.
In Germany, the collective "GenZ regelt" ("Gen Z has got this") says it expects 15,000 people to join protests in Berlin, alongside actions in dozens of other cities.
The protests in European countries were inspired by French students who began blocking their high schools in mid-September to demand better learning conditions.
The school movement fuelled a nationwide campaign against soaring prices, inadequate public services and police brutality. Several young people have lost eyesight or hands to police weapons in the protests and thousands have complained about the severe effects of tear gas.
It has encouraged similar student actions in countries including Belgium, Italy and Spain, where the French word "blocus" (blockade) has become a popular hashtag.
"We are seeing youth movements emerge across the world at the same time," said French historian Sylvain Boulouque.
"What unites almost all of these demonstrations is distrust of law enforcement and political authorities."
(FRANCE 24 with AFP)

items.title: Islam set to be the largest religion by 2035: Where will most Muslims live?
items.summary:
Islam set to be the largest religion by 2035: Where will most Muslims live?
Pew Research projects the Muslim population in Pakistan will overtake Indonesia by 2070, with India second and Nigeria third.
Muslims are projected to outnumber Christians worldwide by 2035, according to projections released
items.text:
Islam set to be the largest religion by 2035: Where will most Muslims live?
Pew Research projects the Muslim population in Pakistan will overtake Indonesia by 2070, with India second and Nigeria third.
Muslims are projected to outnumber Christians worldwide by 2035, according to projections released by the Pew Research Center.
Both religions will keep growing. Between 2020 and 2070, the number of Muslims is expected to rise by 80 percent, from 2.02 billion to 3.64 billion. Christians are projected to grow by 30 percent to 2.96 billion, roughly in step with the world population.
Which religions are growing fastest?
Muslims are projected to grow faster than any other major religious group. Hindus and Jews are expected to grow more slowly than the world population, while the number of Buddhists and people with no religion is projected to shrink.
The main reason is birth rates. Between 2020 and 2025, Muslim women had an average of 3.1 children, compared with 2.5 for Christian women and 1.6 for all other women. A population needs about 2.1 children per woman to replace itself.
Births minus deaths are projected to add 1.6 billion Muslims and 792 million Christians by 2070.
Which countries will have the most Muslims?
Most of the growth will happen where Muslims are already the majority. The 53 Muslim-majority countries are expected to gain 1.2 billion Muslims by 2070, 74 percent of the global increase.
Indonesia had the world’s largest Muslim population in 2020, at 239 million. Pakistan, just 12 million behind, is projected to take the top spot. Pew’s figures compare 2020 with 2070, so they do not say exactly when, but with Pakistan’s Muslim population set to double to 461 million while Indonesia’s grows 15 percent, the switch is likely to come well before 2070.
By 2070, India’s Muslim population is projected to rise from third to second, growing from 213 million to 334 million. Nigeria jumps from fifth to third, more than doubling to 282 million and pushing Indonesia to fourth.
Four of the top 10 in 2070 are in Africa: Nigeria, Egypt, Ethiopia and Sudan. Ethiopia and Afghanistan join the list, replacing Iran and Algeria, while Sudan’s Muslim population more than doubles to 116 million and climbs above Turkiye.
Pew’s projections cover 201 countries and territories, home to 99.98 percent of the world’s population. They assume current trends in fertility, mortality and religious switching continue, and could change with wars, disasters or economic shifts.

items.title: Brown: McLaren wouldn't trade Norris for anyone else on F1 grid
items.summary:
Lando Norris: McLaren chief Zak Brown says he wouldn't trade 2025 world champion for any other driver on F1 grid
Lando Norris has claimed three race victories this season despite McLaren having failed to maintain the level that had brought them successive constructors' titles; watch the Las Vegas GP
items.text:
Lando Norris: McLaren chief Zak Brown says he wouldn't trade 2025 world champion for any other driver on F1 grid
Lando Norris has claimed three race victories this season despite McLaren having failed to maintain the level that had brought them successive constructors' titles; watch the Las Vegas GP on Sky Sports F1, with qualifying at 4am on Saturday and the race at 4am on Sunday
Friday 20 November 2026 08:01, UK
McLaren chief Zak Brown says he would not want to trade Lando Norris for anyone else on the Formula 1 grid.
Norris last year claimed McLaren's first Drivers' Championship since 2008 but has arguably performed even more impressively this season despite sitting sixth in the standings with three races remaining.
Having come out on top last year in a tight battle with his team-mate Oscar Piastri and Red Bull's Max Verstappen, Norris has dominated the Australian this season, with his third grand prix victory of the season last time out in Brazil extending the gap between them to 94 points.
- Las Vegas GP: UK schedule and how to watch on Sky Sports
- F1 2026 Calendar | F1 2026 Standings | F1 Gossip Column
- Got the Sky Sports app? Sign up for latest F1 alerts📱
- Not got Sky? Latest Sky Sports deals or stream F1 with no contract 📺
Asked by Sky Sports F1 at this weekend's Las Vegas Grand Prix about Norris' level of performance, Brown said: "I think he's never driven better. He's driving with a lot of confidence.
"I think the biggest thing I've noticed with Lando this year, when we have a bad session, how quickly he recovers, and he leads himself and the team forward, so I do think he's driving with another year's experience.
"I think Brazil was an amazing drive. Ranking drivers is always difficult. What I would say is I wouldn't want to trade him for anyone else on the grid."
'Verstappen as good as anyone we've ever seen in F1'
Despite his position on Norris, Brown offered high praise to Verstappen during the same press conference.
The four-time world champion was briefly linked to McLaren this summer before committing his future to Red Bull with a new long-term deal.
Verstappen almost overturned a huge deficit to win last year's championship, and has produced another spectacular turnaround this season to surge up to second in the standings behind Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli, who was crowned champion earlier in November.
"He's an unbelievable talent," Brown said of Verstappen. "He's as good as anyone I think we've ever seen in Formula 1, never really makes mistakes, tricky conditions seem to play his way."
Verstappen finished second to Norris in Brazil earlier in November despite starting from the back row of the grid after receiving a penalty for taking a new engine.
Brown continued: "And so look at Brazil again. There are a lot of drivers, if they take a penalty or they start at the back, you can go, 'we don't have to worry about them today'.
"But I think when it's Max Verstappen, as long as he's on the racetrack, you need to worry about him.
"So he's just an awesome, awesome driver. It's great to watch him race, and I also like that on his weekends off he still goes in races, so he's a proper racer, and I think he's a talent unlike many we've seen before."
'Piastri is looking forward to next season'
While Norris has impressed, Piastri has struggled to maintain the high standards he set in 2025 by building a considerable lead in the title battle before wilting over the final third of the season.
The Australian has struggled, at least compared to Norris, with the vastly different style of the all-new cars introduced for the 2026 season following a major regulation change.
McLaren are not the only team where there has been a shift in driver performance, with champion Antonelli surprisingly outperforming George Russell, and Lewis Hamilton faring much better against Charles Leclerc at Ferrari than he had done the previous year.
Brown said: "The cars have been different to drive this year. Some of the driver line-ups have been mixed up from what we saw last year.
"Some drivers, these cars fit their style more than others. Oscar is very brave, especially in the high-speed corners.
"In today's racecars, some corners you might take flat, you have to conserve some battery, so it doesn't allow you to be at the limit in some of the corners he excels at.
"He's much improved and feels much more confident. We are confident. We know how good he is. He will get on top of it shortly."
Pushed on whether Norris has adapted better to the new cars, Brown added: "Lando is as naturally talented as they get. Some drivers take to this stuff quicker than others.
"Oscar's a very good student of data and I have no doubt he will be very strong in the final three races and is looking forward to next season."

items.title: Inside the rise of 'humble' Nyoni and why Iraola trusts him
items.summary:
Inside the rise of 'humble' Nyoni and why Iraola trusts him
- Published
Trey Nyoni knew this was the season when opportunity beckoned for him at Liverpool.
With Curtis Jones leaving for Inter Milan and the club deciding not to buy another midfielder, Nyoni saw the prospect of regular first-team acti
items.text:
Inside the rise of 'humble' Nyoni and why Iraola trusts him
- Published
Trey Nyoni knew this was the season when opportunity beckoned for him at Liverpool.
With Curtis Jones leaving for Inter Milan and the club deciding not to buy another midfielder, Nyoni saw the prospect of regular first-team action if he impressed new head coach Andoni Iraola in pre-season.
First impressions matter. So on the day he returned from a holiday in Morocco in June, Nyoni went from the airport to a personal training session in Leicester - where the 19-year-old grew up and where his family are still based.
Nyoni sought the help of a private football coaching operation as he targeted off-season gains before joining up again with Liverpool.
Coach Steve Stavrou and his son Emillio have also worked with players including Harvey Barnes and Haji Wright. Nyoni asked to work on line-breaking passes, getting away from pressure and improving his finishing.
"We merely supplemented the ability he's already got. He's a quiet and humble lad but knows his ability on the pitch and plays with such a confidence," Emillio Stavrou tells BBC Sport.
Under Iraola, Nyoni has thrived after a stellar pre-season, making 13 appearances already, just one shy of his total appearances last season.
Earlier this month, he scored his first goal for the club in Istanbul.
Liverpool ultimately lost to Fenerbahce in the Champions League that night and Nyoni's belief that "the night has been ruined" showed his inner competitiveness.
His first Premier League start came against last season's champions Arsenal on 1 November.
Nyoni fouled Arsenal's captain early on, leading one source to remark: "He's a nice kid but you saw that steel too with the way he went into Martin Odegaard."
Perhaps the most significant praise came from Liverpool legend Steven Gerrard, who said he couldn't see why Iraola was taking Nyoni off just before the hour mark in that game.
Iraola was managing Nyoni's workload, with the midfielder playing 85 minutes three days later in Turkey.
By now, it is clear that Iraola is unafraid to use him.
"He has to continue in the same place he has been since pre-season: being ready for every game. He is playing all the games lately - so we trust him," said Iraola.
That speaks volumes of Nyoni's rise since joining from Leicester City in 2023 and making his Liverpool debut under Jurgen Klopp as a 16-year-old.
Nyoni, whose parents have Zimbabwean heritage and support Liverpool, is in advanced talks over a new deal.
Having made his England Under-21 debut last week, this is turning into a breakout season with club and country.
Giving Iraola a decision to make
In the summer window, the average spend on a player signed from another Premier League club was £39.4m.
Judging by Liverpool's recent signings - the likes of Alexander Isak (£125m), Bradley Barcola (£123m) and Florian Wirtz (£116m) - there is a sense of satisfaction at the club when the likes of Rio Ngumoha and Nyoni, who cost a fraction of those sums, emerge as first-team options for years to come.
A tribunal decided that Liverpool had to pay Chelsea up to £6.8m in compensation for Ngumoha. In Nyoni's case, Liverpool paid just under £1m in compensation to Leicester.
Nottingham Forest were linked with a £30m move for Nyoni in the summer. Forest denied making the bid, while Liverpool were not interested in a sale.
Iraola saw enough over pre-season to know the teenager would play a prominent part in the new campaign. He only got 237 minutes last season under Arne Slot but has already played 619 minutes this time around.
Slot saw the potential of Nyoni, who trained regularly with the first team. But, given Liverpool's struggles in 2025-26, the Dutchman was reluctant to experiment.
Under Iraola, Nyoni is finding his feet in a deeper midfield role than he had been used to, seeing more of the ball.
"I've been playing like a number six. I played there when I was young, but it's a new position for me. I've had to learn a lot in a short space of time," Nyoni told The Inside Scoop., external
The time he spent before pre-season impressed on the coaches there what a talent Nyoni possessed.
"In the drills, he'd make everything game realistic. Everything was with intent and you see a lot of what he does is with disguise, particularly with his passes," Emillio Stavrou recalls.
With two games a week now the norm for Liverpool, Iraola will continue to rotate his team.
But seeing who he names in midfield against Manchester United on Sunday will be interesting because Nyoni is showing that he can fight for a position alongside the likes of Dominik Szoboszlai, Ryan Gravenberch and Alexis Mac Allister.
Inevitably there is work to be done, particularly in terms of endurance and physicality, in order to cope with the rigours of playing consistently at the top level, but it is so far, so good for Nyoni.
'He is obsessed with getting better'
In a similar manner to Ngumoha's emergence last season, Liverpool were keen not to block Nyoni's pathway, and under Iraola he has been given the platform to thrive.
Liverpool are still only an injury away from looking short of options, so getting another midfielder remains a priority for next summer.
Monaco's Lamine Camara and Bournemouth's Alex Scott are two players of interest.
In the here and now, Nyoni needed this opening. He has come out of his shell and feels a lot more like a part of the squad. That quiet nature is slowly changing and that was visible in an interview he did while on England duty.
Asked how Liverpool are doing by one of the hosts, who supports Manchester United, Nyoni simply responded: "Better than United."
Deep down, there is a young man that backs himself and by all accounts, loves football. Neymar is his favourite player.
"He's obsessed with training and obsessed with getting better. The first session we had with him after he'd just got off the plane tells you about him," adds Emillio Stavrou.

Lionel Messi remains the highest-paid player in Major League Soccer, with $28.3m in guaranteed compensation, according to a s
items.text:
Lionel Messi of Inter Miami tops Major League Soccer salaries
Argentinian football legend Messi, who joined Miami in 2023, signed a contract extension through 2028 last year.
Lionel Messi remains the highest-paid player in Major League Soccer, with $28.3m in guaranteed compensation, according to a salary release on Thursday by the players’ union, with Chicago’s Robert Lewandowski second.
Argentinian legend Messi topped the league list revealed by the MLS Players Association with compensation almost $8m higher than last year, although his figures include only playing compensation, not income from other sources.
Messi signed a contract extension through 2028 last year.
Poland’s Lewandowski, who joined the Chicago Fire earlier this year, was second overall with $19.51m, followed by Orlando’s Antoine Griezmann of France at $13.94m, South Korean star Son Heung-min of Los Angeles FC at $11.15m and Swiss international Breel Embolo of Atlanta United at $10.81m.
Among MLS clubs, Miami topped all teams in total guaranteed compensation at $59.37m, with Chicago second at $41.29m, Atlanta third at $38.35m, the Los Angeles Galaxy fourth at $34.91m and LAFC fifth at $32.91m.
The league’s lowest total team compensation was Philadelphia Union at $12.64m, with Sporting Kansas City second-lowest at $13.30m and DC United third-lowest at $14.55m.
The figures are through October 9 and are annualised for players who arrived in the summer transfer period.

China's Xi praises 'turnaround' in relationship with Australia

Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese and Chinese President Xi Jinping held talks on Friday, following which Xi hailed a "comprehensive turnaround" in the ties between two nations and Albanese said his country was
items.text:
China's Xi praises 'turnaround' in relationship with Australia
November 20, 2026
Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese and Chinese President Xi Jinping held talks on Friday, following which Xi hailed a "comprehensive turnaround" in the ties between two nations and Albanese said his country was engaging "constructively" with Beijing.
The leaders met on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Forum (APEC) summit in China's Shenzhen.
What did Xi say to Albanese?
Xi pointed out to Albanese that they had met four times since the latter became Australia's Prime Minister in 2022.
"I think it is fair to say that together we have brought about a comprehensive turnaround in China-Australia relations," the Chinese President said.
Xi also called for enhancing cooperation in agriculture, energy, the green economy and artificial intelligence, Chinese state news agency Xinhua reported.
Why is China important for Australia?
China is Australia's top trading partner.
The relations between the two countries hit rock bottom under Canberra's former centre-right coalition government, which had called for an independent inquiry into the origins of the coronavirus.
An angry China retaliated by imposing import curbs worth $13 billion (€12.2 billion) on Australian timber, coal, barley, lobsters and wine.
Since Albanese's centre-left Labor party came to power, China has lifted most of its blocks on Australian exports.
But friction in ties has surfaced occasionally on issues such as China conducting a missile test in the South Pacific and Australia tightening a foreign investment screening in the critical minerals sector.
"It is important that Australia continue to engage in a constructive way with China, manage our differences, but not be defined by them," Albanese told the media on Friday.
"What happens in China does matter for Australia," he added.
Iron ore, a pressure point
Albanese is expected to travel to Beijing and meet China's Premier Li Qiang later on Friday.
On Monday, Australia, which is the world's biggest producer of iron ore, called out China's "manipulation" of trade in the commodity over Beijing's formation of a central buying body to purchase ore on behalf of its steelmakers.
A single buyer has increased bargaining power in negotiations with sellers.
Albanese and Li will attend a business roundtable comprising of senior executives from Australian mining giants Rio Tinto and BHP and Chinese company executives.

The 19-year-old England Under-21 international is on a season-long l
items.text:
Moore eyes Kane shirt as Spurs' past and future stars meet
- Published
Cologne loanee Mikey Moore says he hopes to exchange shirts with former Tottenham team-mate Harry Kane when they face Bayern Munich in the Bundesliga on Friday.
The 19-year-old England Under-21 international is on a season-long loan from Spurs, while Three Lions captain and Ballon d'Or winner Kane left north London to join Bundesliga giants Bayern in 2023.
"I haven't actually spoken to him. When he was leaving Tottenham I was just coming into the first team so we don't really know each other too well," said Moore.
"But we've got Bayern on Friday so I'm looking forward to hopefully getting a chat with him and maybe his top."
The 19:30 GMT kick-off will be shown live on BBC Sport and iPlayer.
Kane was still at Tottenham when Moore was first invited to train with the senior squad during the 2021-22 season.
"He's been a massive idol of mine since I was really young," Moore told the Euro Leagues podcast last month.
"When I first went up to train with the first team under Antonio Conte, Harry Kane was over there, and [I saw] some finishing that [I have] never seen anything like again.
"It will be a great experience to play against him and share a pitch with him."
The pair may not have crossed paths in Germany yet but Moore did bump into the England skipper while on international duty last month.
"I'll try my best to get my hands on that shirt," Moore added. "I saw him on the last international break, actually, and went and said hello.
"Hopefully, I'll be coming back to Koln with that in my hand."
'I wanted to take myself a little bit out of my comfort zone'
Moore says the success of Jadon Sancho and Jude Bellingham in the Bundesliga influenced his decision to join Cologne on loan.
Moore's move came almost a decade after a 17-year-old Sancho left Manchester City to join Borussia Dortmund.
During his time in Germany, Sancho established himself as one of Europe's most exciting wingers, making more than 150 appearances for Dortmund and helping the club win the DFB-Pokal in 2021. He subsequently secured a £73m move to Manchester United.
Bellingham followed a similar path in 2020, leaving boyhood club Birmingham City to join Dortmund. The midfielder quickly developed into one of the most sought-after players in world football before joining Real Madrid for an initial £88.5m in 2023.
"Over the years you've seen so many young players come out here, and there are good examples of world-class players like Jude Bellingham and Jadon Sancho doing really well," Moore said.
"It's a really attractive place to play football, especially for a young attacker. It's a great platform to play, and that was sold to me by the people at the club and the manager.
"They've put real trust in me, and the amount of game time I've played so quickly in my Koln [Cologne] career has been nice. It's been good to have that trust from all the staff and people at the club.
"I'm already happy with my decision. Now I can really kick on, make my own story and build my own path in German football."
Although Moore only turned 19 in August, he is no stranger to stepping outside his comfort zone.
Last season, he made 47 appearances in all competitions, including the Champions League qualifying rounds, during a loan spell at Scottish Premiership side Rangers.
It was the first time Moore had left his boyhood club Tottenham, and he rose to the challenge, scoring six goals and providing two assists in 28 Scottish Premiership appearances.
The experience offered a different test to the one he now faces in Germany, but it provided valuable exposure to the demands of first-team football.
"I had options to stay in England and maybe stay somewhere a little more comfortable," Moore said.
"But the conversations came down to me picking a team, and I wanted to take myself a little bit out of my comfort zone to test myself in one of the top five leagues.
"When we were speaking, everyone said they thought it would be a really good experience for me to experience this type of football.
"It's really intense, and there are some great teams in the league.
"For me, it was a no-brainer. I made the decision early that I wanted to come out here, and now I just need to push on."
Having now found an apartment close to fellow England youth internationals Reigan Heskey and Jahmai Simpson-Pusey, who also joined the club this summer, the teenager has turned his attention to learning German.
Moore had his first lesson last month and, at his mother's request, is hoping to expand his vocabulary in the language over the coming weeks.
"I wasn't the brightest at school, so I might take a while to learn the language," Moore joked.
"At least I'll be able to learn a few words so I can order my food in German."

items.title: The Gambia stood up for the Rohingya, now the world must act
items.summary:
The Gambia stood up for the Rohingya, now the world must act
The ICJ has delivered a historic judgement, but justice will depend on what happens next.
There are moments in history when a nation is defined not by its size, wealth, military strength or political influence, but by the courage of its co
items.text:
The Gambia stood up for the Rohingya, now the world must act
The ICJ has delivered a historic judgement, but justice will depend on what happens next.
There are moments in history when a nation is defined not by its size, wealth, military strength or political influence, but by the courage of its conscience.
On Thursday, the International Court of Justice found that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya in northern Rakhine State, in breach of its obligations under the Genocide Convention. For the Rohingya, it is a long-overdue recognition. For The Gambia, it concludes a case our country brought to the Court seven years ago.
The Rohingya have lived in Myanmar’s Rakhine State for generations. Their basic human rights have been systematically denied over time, leaving them stateless and subject to dehumanising rhetoric, hate speech and legal persecution. Following the Myanmar military’s “clearance operations” in 2016 and 2017, over 700,000 Rohingya fled to Bangladesh. The military killed an estimated 10,000 civilians, raped and sexually assaulted women and girls, and burned villages to the ground. There are currently 1.2 million Rohingya refugees in Bangladesh, the majority in the camps of Cox’s Bazar, and 520,000 remain in Myanmar.
When confronted with reports of unimaginable suffering, persecution, displacement and the destruction of communities, The Gambia chose to act. In 2018, our then Minister of Justice, Abubacarr Tambadou, visited the camps in Bangladesh as part of an Organisation of Islamic Cooperation delegation. As a former prosecutor at the International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda, he recognised the signs of genocide in the accounts of the survivors.
With the support of the OIC’s 57 member States, The Gambia brought the case to the International Court of Justice in November 2019. It was the first time in the court’s history that a state with no direct connection to the alleged crimes had filed a case under the 1948 Genocide Convention, which obliges all state parties to prevent and punish genocide wherever it may occur.
Yet, The Gambia’s action before the Court was never only about legal obligations or diplomatic considerations. We asked ourselves one fundamental question: if we remain silent in the face of such suffering, what does our silence make us?
As Gambians, we know the value of dignity. We understand what it means to yearn for justice. We know the pain that comes when our rights are denied, and voices are silenced. Our own history of political struggle taught us that freedom, accountability and human rights are lived realities that shape the lives of us all.
Perhaps that is why this case has resonated deeply with many Gambians: it speaks to our common humanity. In January, Rohingya survivors of the violence testified before the court about what they had lived through. We recognise that the fear of being driven from one’s home knows no nationality, and compassion does not stop at national boundaries.
The years since the case was filed have required patience and perseverance. International justice can often move frustratingly slowly. However, the court’s order in January 2020, the rejection of Myanmar’s objections in 2022, and the interventions from 11 states (Canada, Denmark, France, Germany, the Netherlands, the UK, the Maldives, Slovenia, the DRC, Belgium, and Ireland) on how the Convention should be interpreted have reaffirmed our shared commitment.
The judgement by the world’s highest court today is a reminder that the obligation to prevent genocide applies to every state, large or small, near or far. This is the first time in the history of the court that a state has been found responsible for committing genocide. The court concluded that the widespread rape and sexual violence committed by Myanmar’s security forces were part of the genocide, and that Myanmar failed to prevent genocide and to punish those responsible.
Myanmar is now under a clear obligation to comply fully with the judgement. It is required to investigate and prosecute those responsible, to facilitate the safe, voluntary and dignified return of displaced Rohingya and to protect them from discrimination and persecution. Justice for the Rohingya will also require the restoration of their citizenship and the recognition of their right to be called Rohingya.
Parliamentarians also have a role to play. As the court made clear today, punishing genocide requires laws that explicitly criminalise it. The court has held Myanmar to that standard, and we must hold ourselves to it, too. We must ensure that genocide, crimes against humanity and war crimes are fully incorporated into our domestic laws, and that our courts can try them wherever they are committed.
In our National Assembly, we will ask our government about the next steps, monitor Myanmar’s compliance, and ensure that The Gambia continues to press for that compliance at the United Nations and within the OIC. Other states must now step in by ensuring that Myanmar complies, supporting Rohingya refugees and ensuring they will not be sent back into danger.
As Gambians, we have chosen empathy over indifference, principle over convenience, and action over silence. The Rohingya have shown extraordinary courage and determination in their search for justice, and today international law has finally answered them. Our collective responsibility now is to call for compliance and prevent any future acts of genocide.
The views expressed in this article are the author’s own and do not necessarily reflect Al Jazeera’s editorial stance.

items.text:
EU and Britain to agree steps towards relations reset
A decade after Brexit, London is signalling a willingness to align more closely with the EU on various policies.
British and European Union leaders are set to meet at a summit billed as a chance to reset relations a decade after the Brexit vote.
UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham will meet with European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen and Antonio Costa, who heads the European Council, on Friday in Brussels. In the second such meeting since Britain formally left the bloc in 2020, deals on food, emissions and youth mobility are expected to be sealed.
The previous summit in 2025 was billed as a “stable foundation” upon which to rebuild the relationship between London and Brussels. Friday’s meeting is being sold as a chance to start on a reset of relations.
Burnham said earlier in the week that it was an “obvious truth” that Britain had lost more than it had gained from Brexit, which followed a non-binding referendum in 2016 in which 52 percent of the British public voted to leave the EU. He has signalled that a reformed relationship with Brussels is on his agenda.
The most valuable agreement on the table concerns the cross-border exchange of animals, plants and related products. Britain has estimated that the removal of the current controls could be worth 5.1 billion pounds ($6.7bn) annually.
A potential deal on emissions trading systems could see London and Brussels mutually exempt each other from carbon border levies on goods like steel.
An agreement on youth mobility, which would allow 100,000 people from the EU to live and work for up to three years in the UK, and vice versa, is also reportedly set to be signed. The UK had originally wanted half that number.
The EU is also pushing for students to qualify for “home fees” at British universities – often one third of the international price. London, however, has only agreed to apply “significantly reduced” fees.
The UK also wants to be part of the EU’s “Made in Europe” rules. Brussels has said it may be open to this, but it would require the UK to accept its policies. That could prove tricky for Burnham, given that the UK still hosts a significant Eurosceptic population.

Cricket Australia (CA) should ensure its forum into Sandpapergate is handled as independently and
items.text:
Sandpapergate: Australian gov’t demands CA to ensure transparency in forum
Cricket Australia’s Sandpapergate forum for players to give their accounts has been ridiculed by former cricketers and pundits.
Cricket Australia (CA) should ensure its forum into Sandpapergate is handled as independently and openly as possible, a government spokesperson said on Friday, as former players slammed the governing body’s attempts to defuse an escalating controversy surrounding the 2018 ball-tampering scandal.
CA bosses said on Wednesday that an independent forum would be set up to allow players to give their accounts of the incident, but the results would not necessarily be made public and no sanctions would follow.
The move has been ridiculed by past players and pundits, including former captain Michael Clarke, who said the Australian public had been lied to about who was party to the cheating during the 2018 South Africa Test series.
A spokesperson for Sport Minister Anika Wells said integrity mattered to “every kid with a bat or a ball”.
“This is Cricket Australia’s process to run and it is a matter for them to work through. Australians will expect this to be run independently and as openly as possible,” the spokesperson said in a statement.
“We have a summer of cricket to look forward to and I’m sure all of Australia will get behind our team.”
No prior knowledge
CA did not provide immediate comment when asked by the Reuters news agency on Friday for more details about its forum.
The eight-year-old Sandpapergate scandal has reignited this month following allegations by former Australia batter Usman Khawaja that other players and staff knew of the ball-tampering – not just the three who were found culpable and sanctioned after a rapid investigation by CA’s integrity unit during the South Africa tour.
CA banned then-captain Steve Smith and David Warner for 12 months, and Cameron Bancroft for nine.
Test captain Pat Cummins and fellow pace bowler Mitchell Starc have since rejected Khawaja’s allegations, saying they had no prior knowledge of ball tampering.
But three other players involved in the 2018 tour came forward to back up Khawaja’s account, including Warner and Bancroft, who said “the whole team” knew, including coaching staff and a media manager.
Bancroft claimed the idea to rough up the ball with sandpaper to make it swing was Warner’s, but that the conversation had taken place “within a wider team environment”. He added that he had lied about the extent of the plot to protect CA’s investigation into the incident.
Clarke, who captained Australia from 2011 to 2015, said Bancroft’s explosive 4,000-word statement shared with the media on Wednesday had made CA’s forum redundant.
“The public don’t want any more bullshit,” he said on his podcast, Beyond23.
“The public want the complete truth to allow us to move on.”
The scandal has heaped pressure on Cummins, one of the game’s most devastating pace bowlers, who boasts a strong portfolio of corporate sponsors.
Cummins called Khawaja’s allegations “complete and utter nonsense” in an hour-long news conference last week, and criticised his former teammate for being “casual” with others’ lives and reputations.
He declined to comment to a large media scrum camped outside his Sydney home on Thursday and at training, but his manager said Cummins’s position remained steadfast and he had no need to respond to Bancroft’s statement.
A poll of 13,000 readers of Melbourne’s Herald Sun newspaper had 82 percent saying they believed Khawaja’s, Warner’s and Bancroft’s accounts of Sandpapergate, versus 18 percent for Cummins and Australia’s bowlers who denied prior knowledge.
A majority of 6,000 readers in a poll in the Sydney Morning Herald said they did not expect Cummins to remain as captain for the first Test of the home summer against New Zealand, which starts December 9.
Former Australia bowler Mitchell Johnson said the public pressure on Cummins to stand down as captain would be too much.
“I just can’t see how his captaincy and personal brand survives this,” Johnson wrote in a column for The West Australian newspaper.

NFL: CJ Stroud stars as Houston Texans finally win at home this season with 26-3 defeat of Indianapolis Colts
Houston Texans quarterback CJ Stroud throws for 194 yards and three touchdowns in 26-3 win vs Indianapolis Colts; Stroud picked apart Colts side missing injured starting cornerbacks Sauce Gardner and Charvarius Ward in first Texans home victory this season
Friday 20 November 2026 07:08, UK
CJ Stroud had another big game to help the Houston Texans finally get a victory at home, defeating the Indianapolis Colts.
Stroud threw for 194 yards and three touchdowns as the Texans used a strong defensive performance to coast to a 26-3 win over the Colts.
With the roof at Reliant Stadium open for the first time since 2024, the Texans won a home game for the first time this season after losing their first four.
"To have a home game win is very good for us and exciting," Stroud said. "I think this is a start to something that we need to go on a run with."

- Latest NFL fixtures, results and UK kick-off times
- Get latest Sky Sports deals or stream with no contract
Stroud picked apart a Colts secondary that was missing injured starting cornerbacks Sauce Gardner and Charvarius Ward to help the Texans bounce back from a 27-24 loss to Cleveland last weekend.
It was the third straight game in which Stroud had at least three touchdown passes and the fourth in his last five.
"CJ is producing the way he is producing because of the work he put in throughout the off-season," coach DeMeco Ryans said.
"All of that is paying dividends now. He's been ready for these moments and he's been executing at a high level in these moments."
Stroud gave the Texans a 7-3 lead when he connected with Nico Collins for a 42-yard touchdown late in the first quarter.
Kamari Lassiter intercepted Daniel Jones on the first play of the second quarter. The Texans (4-6) then capped a 12-play, 85-yard drive with a 24-yard TD reception by Kayshon Boutte to extend their lead to 14-3.
The Texans were up by 14 early in the third when Will Anderson Jr sacked Jones in the end zone for a safety that made it 19-3. Anderson leads the NFL with 11.5 sacks and had two tackles in the game to move into first place with 17.
"Obviously, 51 [Anderson] is a problem," Indianapolis coach Shane Steichen said. "We were trying to have a game plan for wherever he was. We were trying to see if he was going right or left. When he was playing right, he was going left. We were trying to keep it away from him as much as we possibly could."
Stroud found rookie Marlin Klein for a 13-yard TD on the next possession.
Ryans was proud of his team for playing a complete game after the Texans fell apart last Sunday against the Browns, blowing a 17-0 lead.
"It's fulfilling to finally see that happen," he said. "We've been in these games a ton where we were up at half-time and come out in the second half and for whatever reason not finish. So for them to actually see it and go do it, I think it will bode well for them to gain confidence for showing that they can do it."
Jones was 12 of 27 for 144 yards with the interception as the Colts (3-8) lost for the sixth time in seven games. Anthony Richardson took over with about seven minutes left and did not complete either of his passes.
Steichen was asked if Jones will remain the starter. "We'll evaluate everything," he said.
The Colts had their worst offensive performance of the season, finishing with a season-low 167 yards and just 38 yards rushing, which was also their fewest this season. They failed to score a touchdown for the first time since a 24-6 loss to Detroit on November 24, 2024.
"I understand where we are as a team," Jones said. "I understand it's an issue to score three points. We have to be better offensively. I am the quarterback, and so, I am responsible. I have to play better. I know that. That's the job."
Houston's David Montgomery had 26 carries for a season-high 107 yards in his return after missing four games with a groin injury.

items.title: UK launches Africa investment platform in Kenya to help businesses grow and create jobs
items.summary:
NAIROBI, Kenya Nov 20 – The UK has launched a new pan-African investment platform in Kenya to help promising businesses attract investors, scale up and create jobs.
UK Minister for Africa Kirsty McNeill announced Forge Africa, a UK-created platform backed by £40 million in investment, during a visit
items.text:
NAIROBI, Kenya Nov 20 – The UK has launched a new pan-African investment platform in Kenya to help promising businesses attract investors, scale up and create jobs.
UK Minister for Africa Kirsty McNeill announced Forge Africa, a UK-created platform backed by £40 million in investment, during a visit to Octavia Carbon’s Project Hummingbird in Gilgil.
The platform will initially launch in Kenya before expanding across Africa and aims to support 100 promising businesses by connecting them with investors willing to provide long-term financing.
Forge Africa is intended to address a funding gap facing ambitious businesses seeking to expand, with the UK saying it will help firms attract investment and create quality jobs.
McNeill said Africa had talented entrepreneurs with the potential to compete in regional and global markets but many struggled to secure the financing and support needed to grow.
“Forge Africa will help close that gap. Starting here in Kenya, it will help promising businesses like Octavia Carbon find investors and create quality jobs,” she said.
She said the initiative reflected the UK-Kenya partnership, with British investment and expertise supporting Kenyan innovation and enterprise.
Octavia Carbon uses geothermal energy from the Rift Valley to remove carbon dioxide from the atmosphere and store it underground. Early UK support helped the company raise about US$10 million and create more than 100 skilled jobs.
UK expands support for Kenyan start-ups
In Nairobi, McNeill also launched the next phase of the Kenya Catalytic Jobs Fund, which links researchers, entrepreneurs, investors, industry and government to turn innovations into businesses.
The new phase will support more than 30 ventures in technology, artificial intelligence, biosciences and women-led technology businesses.
By March 2029, the fund aims to mobilise £50 million in financing for more than 500 start-ups.
British High Commissioner to Kenya Matt Baugh said the initiatives would help businesses move from research and development to commercialisation and expansion.
“Forge Africa and the Kenya Catalytic Jobs Fund will help them take the next step, from the lab to the market, and from start-up to scale-up,” Baugh said.
The first phase of the Kenya Catalytic Jobs Fund supported 19 Kenyan firms, helped create 145,000 direct and indirect jobs and secured an additional £4 million in investment.
The next phase will be led by ISAAA AfriCenter and the Mawazo Institute, alongside partners including Imperial College London, the University of Oxford’s AfOx initiative, BioInnovate Africa and NaiBAN.
Clean energy and investment
During her visit to the Rift Valley, McNeill also toured the UK-backed Globeleq geothermal plant at Menengai, where steam from underground is used to generate electricity and support skilled employment.
Kenya is Africa’s largest producer of geothermal energy, with more than 90% of its electricity coming from renewable sources, according to the statement.
The UK said the Menengai geothermal project and Octavia Carbon demonstrate how the Rift Valley’s natural resources can support clean energy, new industries, skilled employment and efforts to reduce carbon emissions.
In Nairobi, McNeill is also scheduled to meet university students, hear about Kenya’s preparedness and response to the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo, and attend the King’s Birthday Party.
UK-Kenya trade is valued at £2.1 billion annually, while more than 150 British-linked companies support over 250,000 jobs in Kenya.
The initiatives form part of the UK-Kenya Strategic Partnership for 2025-2030, signed in July 2025, which focuses on growth, climate, science and technology, security and migration.

Germany news: Lufthansa to cut 1,000 jobs, reports say
Published November 20, 2026last updated November 20, 2026
What you need to know
- Lufthansa to reportedly slash 1,000 positions at Frankfurt and Munich hubs
- Further Gen Z-led protests are expected across Europe, including in Germany
- German Chancellor Friedrich Merz is set to attend a German-Ukrainian business forum in Berlin
Here's a roundup of the biggest headlines in Germany on Friday, November 20:
President Steinmeier to welcome Emir of Qatar
President Frank-Walter Steinmeier will welcome him the Emir of Qatar Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani in Berlin with military honors.
Steinmeier will also hosting a state banquet for the emir and his delegation in the evening. Al Thani is also expected to meet with Chancellor Friedrich Merz during the day.
The visit comes in the midst of tensions in the Middle East, with the war in Iran likely to be a critical topic in the talks between the two governments. Qatar is currently one of the mediators in the deadlocked conflict between the US and Iran.
Economic and bilateral relations are also expected to take center stage.
On Saturday, the emir will visit Germany's most populous state of North Rhine-Westphalia, where he will be greeted by its state premier Hendrik Wüst at the military section of Cologne/Bonn Konrad Adenauer Airport.
During the visit, Al Thani and North Rhine-Wesphalia leaders will hold an economic conference in the small city of Königswinter, near Bonn, where the Emir will also visit Drachenburg Castle.
Merz to visit German-Ukrainian business forum in Berlin
Following a political summit on Ukraine in Berlin yesterday, the German Chamber of Industry and Commerce (DIHK) said it would host a German-Ukrainian business forum.
Chancellor Friedrich Merz and German Economy Minister Katherina Reiche are expected to be in attendance, along with Ukrainian Prime Minister Sergii Koretskyi, among others.
Christian Bruch, deputy chair of the Eastern Committee of the German Economy and chief executive of Siemens Energy, said German companies are committed to invest in Ukraine, despite Russia's ongoing war and were open to expand their business partnerships.
Bruch said bilateral trade was expected to rise to around €13 billion ($14.1 billion) in 2026.
Lufthansa to slash 1,000 jobs in Frankfurt, Munich — reports
German flagship airline Lufthansa plans to cut 1,000 jobs at its airport hubs in Frankfurt and Munich, according to a company letter seen by German news agency DPA and news outlets.
The letter was reportedly signed by Lufthansa Airlines CEO Jens Ritter and four other managers.
The timeframe of the cuts is unclear. It's also unknown whether the cuts were apart of a previously announced downsizing.
In September 2025, Lufthansa said it would slash 4000 administrative positions due to the implementation of AI and digitalization.
Lufthansa's parent company Lufthansa Group had 67,100 employees in Germany by the end of last year. In the letter seen by news agencies, Lufthansa said financial struggles were the reason behind the planned cuts.
"Lufthansa is currently not competitive in terms of its cost structure, efficiency and productivity," the letter said, while pointing out that the company operated at a €180 million ($197 million) loss in the first nine months of this year.
In addition, Lufthansa Airlines is now in its third straight year of being unprofitable.
In regards to this year, Lufthansa has faced rising fuel costs spurred by the US-Israeli war with Iran, further complicating its financial outlook.

Leaked documents raise new questions about Deutsche Bank's dealings in Russia up to Moscow's invasion of Ukraine, adding to scrutiny over the bank's risk controls and past controversies.
Welcome to our coverage
Guten Tag and welcome to DW's daily coverage of Germany-related news on Friday.
Lufthansa is reportedly planning on cutting jobs as the German flag carrier faces financial difficulties.
Meanwhile, youth-protests are expected across Germany and Qatari's emir is visiting Berlin, where he is expected to meet with German Chancellor Friedrich Merz.
Stay tuned for the latest on all this and more throughout the day from the heart of Europe.

- Lufthansa to reportedly slash 1,000 positions at Frankfurt and Munich hubs
Here's a roundup of the biggest headlines in Germany on Friday, November 20:
Finance ministry launches dialogue on economic future
Germany's finance ministry officials said the agency is launching a dialogue process, dubbed "Germany 2035," to develop proposals for the future
of the country's economy.
Officials want to study how Germany can secure growth and prosperity and what that could look like in terms of fiscal-policy.
Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil will begin the dialogue process on December 2, when he welcomes economists from around the world to Berlin.
Aditionally, think tanks, research organisations, universities and civil society groups have been asked to host workshops, which would take place in the first half of 2027.
Among 12 economic topics that the ministry seeks to explore are tax and fiscal policy, investment and domestic demand, industrial policy, energy and climate transition, foreign trade and sovereignty, and housing and local infrastructure.
The dialogue will culminate with a white paper, to be published in 2028, that can provide recommendations for Germany's economic future up to 2035.
Youth protests expected in German cities
A group called "Gen Z Takes Charge" (Gen Z regelt) has called for thousands of young people to demonstrate in many German cities.
The gathering comes almost three weeks after the first major youth protests hit Germany, inspired by the protests that took place in France in the last weeks.
Those protests, which took place on October 31, saw tens of thousands take to the streets across Germany, with crowds remaining largely peaceful, although rioting broke out in several cities, including Frankfurt, later in the evening.
Among the demands of the "Gen Z Takes Charge" group are increased funding for schools, addiction support and psychotherapy, affordable living, opposition to conscription and consistent action on climate change.
Another group, the Federal Pupils' Conference, has also organized its own demonstration at the Brandenburg Gate in Berlin, with police saying that some 5,000 people have already signed up.
The pupils' conference advocates for improvements in education policy in Germany, including school renovation, school social work, relief for teachers and the inclusion of climate action in curricula.
The demonstrations are set to begin in the morning and run until late afternoon.

items.title: Women farmers earn 18% more per hectare despite smaller farms, FtMA evaluation finds
items.summary:
NAIROBI, Kenya Nov 20 – Women farmers participating in the Farm to Market Alliance (FtMA) programme earn more per hectare than their male counterparts despite farming smaller plots and facing greater resource constraints, according to a nine-year evaluation released in Nairobi.
The evaluation found
items.text:
NAIROBI, Kenya Nov 20 – Women farmers participating in the Farm to Market Alliance (FtMA) programme earn more per hectare than their male counterparts despite farming smaller plots and facing greater resource constraints, according to a nine-year evaluation released in Nairobi.
The evaluation found that women generate an average of KES 82,494 per hectare in main-season revenue, compared with KES 69,833 for men, an 18% difference.
Female farmers in the network cultivate an average of 1.9 acres, compared with 2.8 acres for men. The findings also show that 45% of surveyed women have no formal education, compared with 26% of men.
The report, released at the FtMA National Stakeholder Forum 2026, highlights the gains made in connecting smallholder farmers to agricultural inputs, training and markets, while identifying persistent barriers to financing, mechanisation and market access.
The forum was held under the theme Strengthening Local Food Systems: The FtMA 9-Year Journey and brought together national and county leaders, financial institutions, private-sector off-takers and agripreneurs.
“The data from our nine-year journey proves beyond doubt that when women and young farmers are connected to reliable inputs, agronomic training, and structured markets, they deliver the highest returns per acre in Kenyan agriculture,” said George Njoroge, FtMA Kenya Country Coordinator.
“We must move beyond helping farmers produce more towards enabling them to produce profitably, market competitively, and build resilient livelihoods.”
Programme reaches more than 400,000 farmers
Implemented on the ground since 2017 by the Cereal Growers Association (CGA), with support from the World Food Programme and other partners, FtMA has expanded from two counties to 13.
The evaluation found that the programme operates through 2,126 Farmer Service Centres (FSCs), which have reached approximately 401,955 farmers and marketed 664,009 metric tonnes of produce.
Certified seed adoption stands at 88%, while farmers practising Conservation Agriculture recorded a 60% increase in main-season maize yields, rising from 2.83 to 4.53 metric tonnes per hectare.
The evaluation also found that 95.2% of surveyed farmers can access an FSC within an average distance of two kilometres, while 98.4% of households recorded an acceptable Food Consumption Score.
With agriculture supporting more than 70% of rural livelihoods, the community-based centres are increasingly serving as hubs for agricultural inputs, training, aggregation and market linkages.
Sustainability remains a challenge
Despite the gains, the evaluation found that about 70% of Farmer Service Centres are projected to remain viable after programme support ends.
WFP Kenya Deputy Country Director Bai Mankay Sankoh said sustainability should be built into programmes from the outset rather than considered as funding winds down.
“The ultimate test of our work is not whether a programme can function while we are funding it. It is whether the people, businesses and institutions we have supported can continue to succeed when that funding ends,” he said.
He cautioned that the projected viability rate represents potential rather than proof that the centres will survive without support, citing challenges including working capital, unreliable buyers, financing, business management and access to mechanisation.
“We are not trying to create a permanent network of project-supported centres. We are trying to help build viable rural enterprises that can continue serving farmers because doing so makes commercial sense,” Sankoh said.
Women-led centres face equipment and financing gaps
The evaluation found that women-led Farmer Service Centres own fewer assets than male-led centres, averaging two pieces of equipment compared with 3.2.
Women-led centres also recorded lower average annual profits of KES 143,989, compared with KES 515,253 for male-led centres.
Only 8.5% of centres across the network own shelling or threshing equipment, leaving farmers vulnerable to post-harvest losses. Women can lose up to half of their bean harvest during manual drying, shelling and bagging.
Access to financing remains another challenge. Although 97% of FSCs and 89.4% of farmers have bank accounts, 70% of centres lack formal institutional credit, with agricultural loans often requiring land as collateral.
The centres instead rely on informal borrowing at interest rates of about 20%, while direct credit from buyers or input suppliers reaches only 1%.
Market access is similarly constrained. Although 88.9% of farmers sell their produce, only 3.8% have formal off-taker contracts, and just 18.5% are paid promptly.
Youth increasingly turn to agricultural services
Young people are also emerging as significant participants in the programme, particularly through agricultural service businesses.
The evaluation found that youth under 35 account for 10% of the surveyed farmer sample and 5% of female farmers. Across 1,015 youth-run Farmer Service Centres, each employing an average of 6.1 young people, services include mechanisation, spraying, aggregation and digital agricultural support.
About 91% of youth farmers sell into structured markets, while their main-season maize yields average 3.6 tonnes per hectare, compared with 2.9 tonnes for older farmers.
Youth-run centres lead in digital adoption, at 96%, compared with 92% across the network. However, the cost of mobile data and poor network coverage remain barriers, cited by 73.7% and 43.4% of centres respectively.
Government calls for stronger market linkages
Agriculture Cabinet Secretary Mutahi Kagwe, represented at the forum, said the Farmer Service Centre model was conceived to address gaps in traditional agricultural procurement systems and improve sustainable market access for smallholders.

items.title: Medical professionals sound alarm over antibiotic misuse, warn of rising drug resistance
items.summary: NAIROBI, Kenya, Nov 20 – Medical and pharmaceutical professionals have raised concern over the growing misuse of antibiotics in Kenya, warning that failure to regulate the use of antimicrobial medicines could undermine treatment of common infections and expose the country to a major public health cr
items.text:
NAIROBI, Kenya, Nov 20 – Medical and pharmaceutical professionals have raised concern over the growing misuse of antibiotics in Kenya, warning that failure to regulate the use of antimicrobial medicines could undermine treatment of common infections and expose the country to a major public health crisis.
The Kenya Medical Association (KMA), Kenya Dental Association (KDA) and Pharmaceutical Society of Kenya (PSK) are calling for stricter controls on the sale and prescription of antibiotics, alongside expanded surveillance and public education to contain antimicrobial resistance (AMR).
In a joint statement marking World Antimicrobial Resistance Awareness Week, observed from November 18 to 24, the three organisations warned that drug-resistant infections are increasingly threatening the effectiveness of medicines that have long been relied upon to save lives.
They said Kenya risked losing critical gains in healthcare if urgent measures were not taken to address the inappropriate use of antibiotics in hospitals, pharmacies, communities and the agricultural sector.
The professionals cited global estimates linking bacterial antimicrobial resistance to approximately 4.7 million deaths in 2021, with projections indicating that resistance could directly cause 39 million deaths worldwide between 2025 and 2050.
Africa is expected to experience a particularly heavy burden, raising concerns about the continent’s preparedness to deal with infections that no longer respond to commonly available medicines.
“AMR is one of the greatest threats to global health,” the associations said, urging the government to adopt a coordinated response that brings together the human health, animal health and environmental sectors.
Under the proposed One Health approach, the organisations want interventions targeting antimicrobial resistance to extend beyond hospitals and healthcare facilities to include livestock production, agriculture and environmental management.
They reaffirmed their commitment to supporting Kenya’s National Action Plan on Antimicrobial Resistance, arguing that protecting the effectiveness of existing medicines must become a national priority.
Among the immediate interventions proposed is strengthening infection prevention measures to reduce the need for antibiotics in the first place.
The associations want increased investment in vaccination programmes, improved hand hygiene, better infection prevention and control in healthcare facilities, as well as stronger oral health services.
They also called on medical practitioners, dentists and pharmacists to exercise greater responsibility when prescribing and dispensing antibiotics, insisting that the medicines should only be used when clinically justified.
The organisations further want antimicrobial stewardship programmes expanded to help healthcare workers and patients understand when antibiotics are necessary, how they should be taken and why inappropriate use accelerates resistance.
On regulation, the professionals urged the government to enforce prescription-based access to antimicrobial medicines, warning that uncontrolled sales and self-medication contribute to the growing problem.
They also want diagnostic capacity strengthened to enable healthcare providers to identify infections accurately and select appropriate treatment instead of relying on unnecessary or inappropriate antibiotic prescriptions.
The associations called for expanded surveillance systems to track antimicrobial consumption and resistance patterns, alongside tougher enforcement against the circulation of substandard and falsified medicines.
At the county level, they proposed greater involvement of County Antimicrobial Resistance Focal Persons to coordinate implementation of national interventions, strengthen community awareness and improve accountability.
They further called for infection prevention and oral health measures to be given greater prominence in the country’s antimicrobial resistance strategy.
The three professional bodies also issued a warning to the public against the common practice of purchasing antibiotics without prescriptions, sharing medication or retaining leftover doses for use when similar symptoms arise.
Kenyans were advised to seek medical attention before taking antibiotics and strictly follow instructions from qualified healthcare professionals, including the prescribed dosage and duration of treatment.
They cautioned that unused medicines should not be kept for future illnesses or disposed of carelessly, urging patients to return them to pharmacies for safe disposal.
“Protecting the effectiveness of antimicrobials is a shared responsibility,” the associations said, calling on the government, healthcare professionals, farmers and members of the public to work together to contain the threat.
The 2026 World Antimicrobial Resistance Awareness Week is being marked under the theme, “One Health, One Action: Prevent AMR Now,” highlighting the need for coordinated action across human, animal and environmental health sectors.
Antimicrobial resistance occurs when bacteria, viruses, fungi and parasites evolve and stop responding to medicines designed to treat the infections they cause, making illnesses harder to treat and increasing the risk of disease spread, severe illness and death.

items.title: Live: Deadly Russian attacks damage two bridges in Kyiv, mayor says
items.summary: Russian attacks on Kyiv killed three people and damaged two bridges in the Ukrainian capital, city authorities said on Friday. The fresh wave of missile and drone attacks came after Russian President Vladimir Putin vowed a "painful" retaliation after Ukraine this week damaged the Crimea bridge. Foll
items.text:
Russian attacks on Kyiv killed three people and damaged two bridges in the Ukrainian capital, city authorities said on Friday. The fresh wave of missile and drone attacks came after Russian President Vladimir Putin vowed a "painful" retaliation after Ukraine this week damaged the Crimea bridge. Follow our liveblog for the latest updates.
European troops from 11 countries drill in Poland for a potential postwar Ukraine mission
Thousands of European troops are taking part in an unprecedented military exercise in southeastern Poland to prepare for a potential postwar mission in Ukraine aimed at helping to stabilize the country and rebuild its military once the war ends.
Led by France and the U.K., the multinational force is a non-NATO military initiative of the so-called Coalition of the Willing, a wider political group of 37 nations supporting Ukraine.
The two-week exercise that began on Nov. 9 is for the first time checking this coalition's ability to deploy in Ukraine once the war ends. It is aimed both at testing deployment plans and sending a message to Russia and the Trump administration that European countries are stepping up militarily.
Russia says visit by EU representatives to Russia is 'under consideration'
Russia's deputy foreign minister Sergei Ryabkov said on Friday that a visit by three European Union representatives to Russia is "under consideration", the Russian news agency Interfax reported.
The option of Ukraine joining NATO, even in the form of "quasi-membership", is unacceptable to Russia, Ryabkov said, referring to possible security guarantees for Ukraine under Article 5 of the Washington Treaty.
Ukraine says drones hit 40 Russian oil, military targets in last 50 days
Ukraine's Unmanned Systems Forces have hit 40 Russian oil facilities and defence industry targets over the past 50 days, the forces' commander has said.
In a post on the Telegram messaging app, Robert "Magyar" Brovdi said five targets had been hit more than once. He added that the Dorogobuzh chemical plant in Russia's Smolensk region was struck on November 10 and November 20.
Poland investigating fall of unknown object near Ukraine border
The Polish Army received information about a possible fall of an unknown object approximately 45 kilometers (28 miles) from the border with Ukraine, Jacek Goryszewski, spokesman for the Armed Forces Operational Command, told TVN24.
"The services were informed by residents, and a ground team was dispatched to secure the area and locate the site, if indeed the fall occurred there," he said, adding that an investigation is ongoing.
Ukraine attack damages industrial facility in Russia's Smolensk, governor says
A Ukrainian drone attack damaged an industrial facility in Russia's western region of Smolensk, Governor Vasily Anokhin said on Friday on the Telegram messaging app, without identifying it.
Russian strikes hit Kyiv region and northeast Ukraine, local officials say
A building in the Obolon district and a building in the Podil district, both in the Kyic region, were set ablaze after Russian attacks, the capital's military administration said.
In the northeastern city of Kharkiv, mayor Igor Terekhov said on Friday that a Russian drone damaged a hospital.
"Four people were wounded, and more than 50 windows were blown out," he said on Telegram.
Terekhov also reported a fire at a residential complex in the city's Shevchenkivsky following an attack.
Emergency power cuts introduced in Ukraine's Lviv, city official says
Russia hits sea vessels, energy and transport facilities in Ukraine
Russia's Defence Ministry said its forces hit defence industry facilities, as well as energy and transport infrastructure, in several regions including the Ukrainian capital of Kyiv.
Also hit were port infrastructure facilities in the Odesa region and sea vessels used for Ukrainian military purposes, the ministry added.
Poland verifies radar data after suspected airspace violation, army says
Polish airport suspends flights as military aircraft activate
Polish airport in Rzeszow suspended flight operations due to the activation of military aircraft, the Polish Air Navigation Services Agency (PANSA) said on X.
The Polish Air Force is conducting preventive operations related to Russian missile attacks on Ukraine, the Polish army said in a post on Friday.
Russian attacks kill three in Kyiv, city military administration says
Russian attacks killed three people in Kyiv, the city's military administration said on Friday, as Moscow launched a fresh barrage of drones and missiles against Ukraine.
"Unfortunately, three people were killed in the enemy attack on the capital... two people were also wounded," Kyiv's city military administration said on Telegram.
At least another 15 were reported wounded, he said.
Russian strikes damage two bridges in Kyiv, mayor says
Russian attacks damaged two of Kyiv's bridges, the mayor of the Ukrainian capital Vitali Klitschko has said, as Moscow launched a fresh wave of missiles and drones.
"As a result of the ballistic attack on the capital, the Podilsko-Voskresensky Bridge crossing has been damaged. Traffic from the right bank to the left bank is currently closed on it. The Darnytsky Bridge has also been damaged," Klitschko said on Telegram.
He added that the Southern Bridge was hit but did not specify if it was damaged.
Welcome to the FRANCE 24 liveblog covering the war in Ukraine.
China's Xi Jinping, Russian President Vladimir Putin and his US counterpart Donald Trump met for a historic summit in Shenzhen, China, on Thursday where Putin said the three countries had "numerous shared interests in the settlement of regional conflicts, including obviously the conflict in Ukraine".

items.title: Nigeria moves to end jail terms for attempted suicide
items.summary:
Nigeria moves to end jail terms for attempted suicide
- Published
Nigerian President Bola Tinubu has asked parliament to decriminalise attempted suicide, proposing medical support instead of prosecution for those who survive.
The proposal seeks to shift Nigeria's approach from criminal punishment to
items.text:
Nigeria moves to end jail terms for attempted suicide
- Published
Nigerian President Bola Tinubu has asked parliament to decriminalise attempted suicide, proposing medical support instead of prosecution for those who survive.
The proposal seeks to shift Nigeria's approach from criminal punishment to treatment and rehabilitation.
It follows years of calls for reform from mental health professionals. A separate bill seeking to decriminalise attempted suicide has already passed its second reading in the Senate.
Under Nigeria's law, attempted suicide is a criminal offence with those convicted facing up to one year's imprisonment, a fine or both.
The Senate bill also seeks to replace criminal penalties for attempted suicide with medical treatment, rehabilitation and support.
It was sponsored by Senator Asuquo Ekpenyong, who has argued that prosecuting people who survive suicide attempts could discourage those experiencing suicidal thoughts from seeking help.
He also warned that families might conceal such incidents for fear of prosecution and social stigma.
He stressed that the bill is not aimed at legalising or encouraging suicide attempts but rather protecting the survivors.
Tinubu's proposal has been welcomed by Senate President Godswill Akpabio, who had previously suggested that people who survived suicide attempts should be sent to prison.
"We are saying that suicide is a crime for now. Therefore, if you attempt it, we will send you to prison," Akpabio had said.
However, after receiving the Tinubu's proposal, he sought to clarify his earlier remarks, saying they did not apply to people experiencing mental health conditions.
He added that punishing people whose actions were influenced by mental health conditions would be insensitive.
Tinubu's letter follows sustained calls from mental health professionals for the law to be changed.
At a parliamentary public hearing in May 2024, the then president of the Association of Psychiatrists of Nigeria, Professor Taiwo Obindo, urged lawmakers to remove criminal penalties for attempted suicide.
"Why do we, as a nation, then punish individuals who are ill and need medical attention rather than prosecution?" he asked.
Drawing on his experience as a psychiatrist, Obindo said most people who die by suicide have a history of mental illness.
Akpabio has referred the president's amendment bill to the relevant senate committee for further consideration.
Nigeria is among several African countries where attempted suicide remains a criminal offence.
Ghana decriminalised attempted suicide in 2023, while Kenya's High Court ruled in January 2025 that the law criminalising it was unconstitutional.
