items.title: Anthropic becomes one of world’s most valuable public companies in stock market debut
items.summary:
NEW YORK, United States, Nov 20 — Anthropic has become one of the most valuable public companies in the world after its shares began trading on the stock market, taking its valuation to roughly $1.76 trillion (£1.34 trillion).
The artificial intelligence (AI) company’s Thursday debut on the Nasdaq s
items.text:
NEW YORK, United States, Nov 20 — Anthropic has become one of the most valuable public companies in the world after its shares began trading on the stock market, taking its valuation to roughly $1.76 trillion (£1.34 trillion).
The artificial intelligence (AI) company’s Thursday debut on the Nasdaq stock exchange was a crucial test for the industry, given the huge amount of money being poured into advancing the technology.
Anthropic’s shares flew past its allocation price of $83 each, showing there was plenty of excitement around AI.
Yet the company, which is behind AI chatbot Claude, will remain under intense scrutiny in the months ahead to answer the key question surrounding AI: is it all worth it?
In just a few hours of trading, Anthropic’s stock seemed to show that investors remain uncertain of where exactly AI is heading. The share price rose immediately to $111.53, sending the company’s market value to almost $2 trillion, before falling by the end of the day as the shares closed at $97.17.
Some investors said Anthropic’s debut seemed to be a success, as shares rose roughly 17% during the day, but the broader tech market did not perform as well.
The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite Index closed down nearly 2.3%. Stocks fell in the largest tech firms, including Google’s parent company Alphabet, which was down by 2.9%, while Amazon lost almost 3.9%.
The buildout happening around this era of AI is among the most expensive endeavours in the history of technology, with more than $1 trillion being spent in the last year alone by a handful of major tech companies.
The speed at which investment has grown has led to ongoing concerns of a financial bubble.
“Bubbles don’t burst on the day of the largest deal,” Richard Whittle, an economist with the University of Salford said. “They burst later, if the positive future becomes suspect.”
While the basics of the technology have been around for decades, the more recent advent of more powerful computers and related components have allowed the processing of more data than ever.
The result has been AI chatbots that simulate human speech and operate tasks like software coding, digital image generation, and searching the internet more quickly.
It represents a new way of using computers that has led to the rapid rise of Anthropic, which started just five years ago and is best known as the maker of the popular AI chatbot Claude.
As the first purely AI company to go public, Anthropic will almost certainly see significant swings in price on the stock market going forward, according to Ben Barringer, who leads technology research at Quilter Cheviot.
The “initial exuberance” will wear off, Barringer said, pointing to what happened with SpaceX earlier this year.
That company, led by Elon Musk, saw shares jump by about 10% on the first day of trading, taking the company to a record-breaking valuation of $2.2 trillion.
Within a month shares had fallen below their debut price, and have mostly fallen further since.
Most tech companies see their shares fall after hitting the stock market, often after reporting quarterly results for the first time.
But many such companies, including Meta, Amazon and Google, have gone on to become the largest and most profitable corporations in the world.
With Anthropic, investors are not only looking at a notable tech company with a major valuation, and a potentially big future in business, but a company that is the first of its kind on the stock market.
“There’s no obvious peer to compare it to,” Neil Wilson, an investor strategist at Saxo UK, said.
Simon Jack: Can Anthropic’s record-breaking IPO stop the AI bubble bursting?
Daniela Amodei: Anthropic and the price of AI
So, as individual investors and even researchers and investors at large funds ask themselves if Anthropic is really worth more than $1.7 trillion, or even more, there will be few answers available.
“We’ll have a stab at it,” Wilson said. “I don’t think anyone really knows.”
A few things will likely impact the company’s success on the stock market in the near-term.
One of those things is the prospect of new laws governing the use of AI tools. In the US, where Anthropic is based, Democrats will be in many more positions of power come 2027, and several politicians have already said they will be looking to ensure AI tools are safe and have some guardrails attached.
Such regulation is currently unlikely at the federal level. US President Donald Trump on Thursday spoke about AI during the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in China, alongside Chinese and Russian counterparts, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin.
Trump reiterated his position against “any form of robust regulation” around the technology, adding, “we won’t allow that to happen, frankly.”
The same day, however, a bipartisan group of US lawmakers formed the House AI Safety and Innovation Caucus, which will work specifically on AI regulation and safety considerations.
A significant driver of this kind of scrutiny is Anthropic itself. Company executives, including co-founder and CEO Dario Amodei, have been outspoken in their purported fears that future AI tools will become so capable they will outsmart humans, to the point where extinction is possible.
Anthropic has always put itself forward in public as an AI company that takes the safety of its technology very seriously.
Daniela Amodei, Anthropic’s president and sister of Dario Amodei, boasted on Thursday that the company “had an AI safety team before we launched our first product”.
“AI carries real risks,” she added.
Despite the company’s claims that the technology it is building at a rapid pace could be dangerous, Anthropic has made one of the quickest trips from start-up to IPO in history.

items.text:
‘We don’t want our future decided by the military’: Young Germans protest
Ahead of Friday’s nationwide rallies, two German teenagers explain why they are resisting conscription and growing militarisation.
Berlin, Germany – Last month, high school student Phil Werring received a letter from the German Armed Forces, known as the Bundeswehr.
In an official document, a military registration form, Werring was asked to answer compulsory questions – and optional ones if he was interested in joining the army.
After initially ignoring the first letter, two weeks later he received another, warning him of a 250 euro ($275) fine if he did not answer.
Logging in via a QR code, he started working his way through the questionnaire.
“The mandatory questions included ones on whether you have any diseases, your weight, height and whether you played sports, while other questions asked about whether you had a driving licence and what languages you spoke,” the 18-year-old, who lives with his three younger siblings and parents in Muenster, western Germany, told Al Jazeera.
“I only answered the mandatory questions, so it took me around 15 minutes to complete, but if I had filled it all out, it would have taken me a lot longer. I know that not answering all the questions can increase my chances of being called in by the military for a check-up, but I still didn’t want to answer them all.”
Official figures show that by the end of October, nearly 600,000 letters had been sent out this year to young Germans, of which about 286,800 were sent to young men and 271,700 to women and people of other genders. The form is only mandatory for men to complete.
Military conscription, meanwhile, has been a headline-grabbing issue in Germany since the start of the year, after the Military Service Modernisation Act came into effect on January 1 . It set out new targets to grow the army by the mid-2030s, increasing its full-time force to about 260,000, plus 200,000 reservists.
The recruitment drive is one element of Germany’s broader military expansion plans, initiated in 2022 after Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine. Berlin is also increasing defence budgets and surveillance powers for intelligence services.
According to the Ministry of Defence, its efforts are yielding positive results. Official figures indicate that the Bundeswehr has already exceeded the statutory force build-up range for 2026, with personnel numbers in October about 6,400 higher than the same month last year.
Yet as recent protests have shown – including a series of school strikes and a large-scale demonstration organised by a loose alliance called “Gen Z Regelt” (Gen Z Sorts It) – many young people are pushing back against the plans.
Gen Z Regelt is rallying again on Friday, with nearly 20,000 people across 40 cities, including Berlin, Cologne, Frankfurt and Munich, signed up so far.
“The military questionnaire had many personal questions, and I found the experience quite scary, and it made me angry,” Werring said. “As I filled out the form, I realised how serious the government is about taking these steps to reintroduce compulsory military service, and that I may have no choice but to serve and risk my life for companies making millions selling arms. It made me realise that I must be active against these steps towards militarisation and support resistance efforts against these war preparations.”
‘Students worry about the roof falling on them’
Linus Schneider, 16, fears that as more money goes towards rearming Germany, the less there is for schools like those in his home city of Munich, which are not in good shape.
“The roofs have been leaking at my school for three years now,” he told Al Jazeera. “Something wasn’t installed properly when the building was built a few years ago, and the city has been saying that they don’t have as much money as they did a few years ago, so they can’t fix the issue. This has led to a lot of problems at school; for example, sometimes we can’t have gym class at all because there are buckets of water in the sports hall.”
Munich is the largest city in one of Germany’s wealthiest states, Bavaria.
Schneider added, “I also hear from friends in other schools that their roofs are in such a bad condition that they are worried about the roof falling on them. We literally don’t have good roofs over our heads. There are big cuts to education and healthcare, while at the same time, military spending has increased drastically.”
According to the current draft budget for 2027, to be agreed on later this month, defence spending is expected to rise to 109.7 billion euros ($120.5bn) from 82.7 billion euros ($90.8bn) the year before. The Ministry for Education and Family, meanwhile, projects a budget of 15.9 billion euros ($17.5bn) compared to 16.6 billion euros ($18.3bn) this year.
Sebastian Koos, a sociologist at the University of Konstanz who researches youth and protest movements, said the wave in Europe was an “important spark” for the German movement.
“There are some similarities and overlaps with the problems, such as the cost of living and cuts to education. But I think the issue of military conscription makes the situation for young people here unique,” he told Al Jazeera.
Koos said that while several different organisations participate in the Gen Z Regelt protests, a common thread is a sense of hopelessness.
“There are also many issues and demands that are being put together. They are also worried about economic and social inequality, right-wing extremism, the cost of living, as well as climate change. This is a lot to digest, and it is very difficult to get a sense of hope if you are confronted with so many different conflicts.”
Friday’s protest will include thousands of students protesting against compulsory military service, organised by the youth-led alliance, School Strike Against Conscription.
Werring will be among those taking to the streets in his local area.

Araujo, 27, joined the Premier League side in the summer and has impressed so far, scoring two goals in 15 appearances across all competitions.
Dec
items.text:
Barcelona sporting director Deco has said the Spanish champions would welcome the money if Liverpool decide to sign Ronald Araujo beyond his loan spell.
Araujo, 27, joined the Premier League side in the summer and has impressed so far, scoring two goals in 15 appearances across all competitions.
Deco is pleased to see the Uruguayan defender enjoying himself in England, but says Barça would be happy to see Liverpool execute the €55 million option to make the move permanent.
"I am happy for him," Deco told Catalunya Radio when asked about Araujo's positive start at Anfield.
"We work for Barcelona and want what's best for the club -- to win, to build the best possible squad -- but we are also humans and we also want to build relationships.
"Ronald's been one of the club captains in recent years. He has had difficult moments, but also moments of great happiness and he has been one of the leaders of this team.
"Coming back to the football, things weren't going especially well for him on the pitch. He took the decision [to join Liverpool] and we respect it. The most important thing for us now is seeing Ronald recovered, happy, enjoying himself and in a positive place.
"If he decides to stay, Liverpool have an option to make the deal permanent. They would also have to negotiate with him -- it's not just about paying the clause -- but we would be happy for several reasons [if the deal goes through].
"Firstly, because the move has worked out and because Ronald is happy and is able to continue his career successfully. We want players to succeed. Also, the money would not hurt, either."
Deco confirmed there is a deadline for Liverpool to decide if they will pay the €55 million stipulated in the agreement between the clubs to bring Araujo in full time.
However, he suggested Barça could allow some leeway when it comes to talks over the timing of any deal and the final fee.
"In football, you can always negotiate," he added. "There is a deadline for exercising the option, just as there is when we bring players in on loan.
"After that, you can always try to negotiate and work things out. It will depend on the circumstances at the time, on us, on the player and on various other factors."
- O'Hanlon: 10 Best: Ranking the world's top men's footballers ... again!
Deco on Alejandro Balde's 'uncomfortable situation'
Deco, however, denied Barça are pushing left-back Alejandro Balde out the door.
Balde, 23, has been restricted to just five appearances this season for a total of 124 minutes, with João Cancelo, Xavi Espart and Gerard Martín all preferred ahead of him in recent games.
"He's in an unconformable situation," Deco acknowledged. "But he's come through at the club and has been, and is, an important player.
"He's not playing as much right now, but there's no plan to transfer Balde. He's at the start of his career. Of course it also depends on the player, but he's not told us anything."

items.title: FIFA presidential challenger Tashima willing to unite with Diallo against Infantino
items.summary:
TOKYO -- Kohzo Tashima said he hasn't talked yet with Philippe Diallo, but he's willing to work with the Frenchman to defeat Gianni Infantino's bid for a controversial fourth term as the president of FIFA, soccer's world governing body.
Tashima and Diallo are two long-shot candidates to replace Infa
items.text:
TOKYO -- Kohzo Tashima said he hasn't talked yet with Philippe Diallo, but he's willing to work with the Frenchman to defeat Gianni Infantino's bid for a controversial fourth term as the president of FIFA, soccer's world governing body.
Tashima and Diallo are two long-shot candidates to replace Infantino in an election set for March 18. So there's still plenty time to sway FIFA's 211 member federations, which now seem to be leaning toward Infantino.
"We do share some moral or ethical positions, so he's a great person to team up with," Tashima said Friday at a 40-minute news conference. His comments were translated from Japanese. "I'm not looking at Diallo as opposition. I just want to change FIFA."
"Diallo is also very strict in governance and he does have a lot of experience in management," Tashima added. "I do trust him. At this point I'm not think about withdrawing."
Tashima is going against the endorsement of the Asian Football Confederation, which last month in a conference in Tokyo pledged support for Infantino - with Infantino on hand. The AFC is headed by Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa of Bahrain.
Tashima repeated the words "integrity, fairness, trust and transparency" over and over as he explained why he decided to run. Tashima is well-known inside the soccer world, but has little profile outside.
"I just don't only want to be the FIFA president, my intention was to make FIFA better," Tashima said. "Being the president is the shortcut to making that happen. I just want to clean up the federation and make it a fair organization. I want to help rebuild the whole organization."
Tashima is the former president of the Japan Football Association -- now honorary president -- and one of 37 people who sit on the FIFA Council, FIFA's ruling committee.
He said comments in some media about him being -- in his words -- "unflashy" should be considered a positive endorsement.
"That's OK. I don't have to be in the spotlight. It's the players," he said.
Tashima has been critical of Infantino, which he made clear when he declared his candidacy on Nov. 5.
"I believe the worst outcome would be for him (Infantino) to remain in office without an election," Tashima said. "I believe this is a test of whether FIFA truly has the capacity for self-reform."
Infantino had initially been expected to be re-elected unopposed. But he has faced harsh criticism over a reported plan to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors.
"He's done a lot of things to make us doubt his integrity," Tashima said Friday, adding that income from the World Cup - or anywhere else - "is not an Infantino asset. It belongs to FIFA."
Tashima acknowledged being at a handicap in the election, but he repeated the worst scenario "is Infantino running for another term without opposition."
Infantino earned close to $6 million last year at current exchange rates.
In a three-candidate election, votes from two-thirds of the eligible members are needed to win in the first round. For the second round, the candidate with the fewest votes is eliminated and a simple majority will win.
In a two-candidate race, Infantino would need votes from 106 of the 211 member federations to win re-election.
An unofficial tally by The Associated Press shows he has 105 votes based on announcements by member federations before nominations for the election closed. The actual vote is secret.

items.title: Rodman eyes 'full-circle moment' with NWSL title: 'Would mean everything'
items.summary:
WASHINGTON -- Washington Spirit forward Trinity Rodman said it would mean "everything" to win another NWSL Championship on home soil at Audi Field on Saturday, especially after the contract saga that surrounded her at last year's championship.
"It would mean everything," Rodman told Futbol W, ESPN's
items.text:
WASHINGTON -- Washington Spirit forward Trinity Rodman said it would mean "everything" to win another NWSL Championship on home soil at Audi Field on Saturday, especially after the contract saga that surrounded her at last year's championship.
"It would mean everything," Rodman told Futbol W, ESPN's weekly women's soccer studio show, at NWSL Championship Media Day on Thursday. "And I think it's just like, full-circle moment obviously with it being in D.C.
"But just starting my pro career here and then re-signing to stay and play here, everything that I've been through just with the fans here, the community, everything, and how much the fan base has grown. To be able to do that in this city will be the most rewarding thing and very celebratory. I'm hoping that we're able to celebrate with the fans after this."
Washington will play the Kansas City Current on Saturday in the league's 13th title match.
Rodman won the NWSL Championship with the Spirit as a rookie in 2021. The Spirit lost the past two finals, to the Orlando Pride in 2024 and to Gotham FC in 2025. Rodman was dealing with injuries both times, first to her back in 2024 and then to her knee last year.
The USWNT star stayed healthy this season and had a career year, scoring 12 goals and adding eight assists in the regular season. She has two goals and two assists in two playoff games so far this year.
"You, as an athlete, sometimes don't realize how just rewarding life and games are until you're injured and you're like, 'Woah, I miss this, I wish I was on the field," Rodman said.
"So, not to keep talking about the injury, but it has really helped me develop as a player and zoom out a little bit. I think that's the reason that I've performed so well, because I'm not overthinking, not putting this crazy amount of pressure on myself. I'm just genuinely happy and grateful to be on the field."
Earlier Thursday, during her annual state of the league address, NWSL commissioner Jessica Berman said it was "poetic" that Rodman was back in the final after what transpired last year.
Rodman entered last year's NWSL Championship as an impeding free agent who was attracting lucrative offers from Europe that the Spirit could not match within the confines of the NWSL's salary cap. In December 2025, the NWSL Board of Governors ratified the High Impact Player rule, also known as the Rodman Rule, to allow teams to pay star players larger salaries outside of the salary cap.
Rodman and the Spirit were the first team and player to utilize the rule. Rodman signed a contract worth over $2 million annually on average, making her the highest paid player in the NWSL and, as ESPN reported at the time, the world.
"The fact that she's competing in the championship again is poetic, given how far we've come and all the progress we've made," Berman said. "It's no secret that the next generation of fans appreciates and enjoys stars, and Trinity's done an incredible job of building her celebrity off the field.
"And we are excited that she brings that to our game. It makes people want to watch. It makes people want to follow her and her stories."
The Spirit are appearing in their fifth NWSL final, tying the record set by the Western New York Flash/North Carolina Courage franchise. They have won once and lost three times.
The Kansas City Current are playing in their second NWSL Championship after losing the 2022 edition to the Portland Thorns, also at Audi Field.
After the final, Rodman will join up with the United States for a quarterfinal match against El Salvador as part of the Concacaf W Championship. Emma Hayes would clinch a spot in the 2027 World Cup in Brazil with a win.

items.text:
Forward Daryl Dike suffered an injury in Orlando City SC's 3-1 defeat to FC Cincinnati in the Major League Soccer playoff wild card match on Thursday night at Inter&Co Stadium in Orlando, Florida.
Dike entered the playoff match in the 75th minute before suffering the injury moments later.
"I don't know what the issue is; we haven't been able to, I haven't had time yet to see the doctors, so I don't know exactly what's wrong," interim coach Martín Perelman said in the post-match press conference.
"I think it's something with his hamstring, since that's where he was holding, so I assume he might have some kind of tear or something similar in the hamstring, but I'm not certain. I don't know exactly what it is, but naturally, he's frustrated, just like the rest of us."
Despite the apparent injury, Dike stayed on the pitch for the rest of the game given that Orlando City did not have any more substitution windows available.
"Regarding the substitutions, these are things that can happen, and they're difficult to predict," Perelman said.
"You never expect a player to come on with 15 minutes left and then get injured; that's not something you anticipate. So, I don't think it's fair to second-guess the substitutions based on that. It simply happened, and that's that-we can't change it now. It was just another piece of misfortune in the match, and, well, as I said, that's part of the game."
Dike has a lengthy injury history, suffering a season-ending hamstring injury in 2022, a right Achilles tendon rupture in 2023, a left Achilles tendon rupture in 2024, and most recently a thigh concern that kept him on the sidelines for 10 matches during the start of the 2025/26 season.
Orlando striker Martín Ojeda opened up the scoring in the 26th minute of the match before goals by Cincinnati players Evander and Samuel Gidi won the game for the visiting side.
Orlando City, in Antoine Griezmann's first season, has now been eliminated from playoff contention.
"We are very disappointed because we wanted to bring happiness to our fans, to our families, and everyone here at the stadium, and we couldn't," said Perelman. "That is frustrating for us, but at the same time, again, the effort was not enough, but it was there. This group of players will bring happiness and achievements to this club."
Cincinnati will now go on to face Nashville SC in the best-of-three round of the playoff series.

items.text:
Inter Miami CF star Lionel Messi remains the highest-paid player in MLS, though the number of players making at least $10 million grew to five.
According to the MLS Players Association, Messi's guaranteed compensation remained $28.33 million, the same as during the spring salary release, though it is up from $20.45 million a year ago. Other players in the over $10 million club include the Chicago Fire FC's Robert Lewandowski ($19.51 million), Orlando City SC forward Antoine Griezmann ($13.94 million), LAFC's Son Heung-Min ($11.25 million) and Atlanta United FC forward Breel Embolo ($10.81 million).
All told, 150 of the league's players make at least $1 million in guaranteed compensation.
As in previous years, Messi's number reflects just the playing portion of his compensation. Last October, Messi signed a contract extension through the 2028 campaign. Inter Miami owner Jorge Mas told Bloomberg in March that Messi's total income is between $70 million to $80 million per year. Messi is also expected to acquire an equity stake in the club once he retires.
All data is as of Oct. 9, 2026. The salary data was annualized for players who arrived during the summer transfer window.
Miami continues to obliterate the competition in terms of total team spending. Thanks in part to the midseason arrival of midfielder Casemiro, Miami increased its spending to a record $59.37 million, though it finished second in the Eastern Conference behind Supporters Shield winners Nashville SC, which spent just $24.97 million. Miami's outlay is more than double the amount spent by 25 of the league's remaining 29 teams.
In terms of team payroll based on guaranteed base compensation, Chicago ranked second behind Miami at $41.29 million, due in part to the midseason arrival of Lewandowski. The Fire were followed by Atlanta United ($38.35 million), the LA Galaxy ($34.91 million) and LAFC ($32.91 million)
The Philadelphia Union had the league's lowest payroll at $12.64 million. Budding star Cavan Sullivan's guaranteed compensation checked in at a relatively modest $614,000. The next lowest payrolls after the Union were Sporting Kansas City ($13.30 million), D.C. United ($14.55 million), CF Montreal ($15.02 million) and FC Dallas ($15.49 million).
The average guaranteed base compensation for the entire MLS player pool -- which included pool players and retired players still owed money -- continues to climb on an annual basis, rising to $746,936, up 18% from the October 2025 mark of $632,809.
The salaries of players at the bottom of the wage scale continue to improve, though not at the same rate as those at the top. The league's median guaranteed base compensation was $360,042, up 6.4% from the October 2025 mark of $338,347.
MLS and the MLSPA are in the sixth year of the collective bargaining agreement (CBA) that was agreed upon in February 2021. The current CBA runs through the end of 2027.

items.title: Pochettino's 1st Man United training session filmed by drone, posted online
items.summary:
Video footage of Mauricio Pochettino's first training session as Manchester United head coach has appeared on YouTube after it was filmed by a drone operator.
Around 12 minutes of the session was posted online on Thursday -- Pochettino's first full day in the job after arriving in Manchester on Wedn
items.text:
Video footage of Mauricio Pochettino's first training session as Manchester United head coach has appeared on YouTube after it was filmed by a drone operator.
Around 12 minutes of the session was posted online on Thursday -- Pochettino's first full day in the job after arriving in Manchester on Wednesday. United have declined to comment.
- Pochettino: Man United players must relearn 'about being winners'
- Predicting the rest of the Premier League season: How all 20 teams will finish
- After a decade of near misses, Man United finally get their man in Pochettino
The footage shows Pochettino -- who signed a two-and-a-half year deal to take over from Michael Carrick last week -- working with a group of players while another two groups work separately under the supervision of his assistant, Jesus Perez.
Audio from the footage of United's Carrington training base could be heard, with the man appearing to operate the drone saying "let's get closer," before zooming in on Pochettino.
Harry Maguire, Kobbie Mainoo, Amad Diallo, Matheus Cunha and Bryan Mbeumo were among the players shown working with Pochettinho.
"I can definitely see Harry Maguire," added the man providing commentary. "That there is Bruno [Fernandes], definitely, [I can] tell by the gestures."
Perez, along with staff members Toni Jimenez and Sebastiano Pochettino, arrived at Carrington earlier in the week after being released from their commitments with the USMNT ahead of Pochettino's final game in charge against Haiti on Tuesday.
The account justified the filming in a pinned post that said it's legal.
"It is unrestricted airspace, meaning anyone can fly over it. The drone remained in line of sight at all times, it didn't fly over anyone or even near anyone," the post said. "The drone is correctly labelled and I hold all the relevant licenses, public liability and insurance required."
The post said no sensitive information had been revealed with regard to how struggling United would line up at fourth-place Liverpool in the Premier League on Sunday.
"As for leaking team news/tactics, it was half an hour into the manager's first training session," wrote the poster. "There are many media there so certainly won't be the only footage of training released."
Pochettino travelled directly from Cincinnati to Manchester immediately after his final match with the USMNT and arrived at Carrington on Wednesday afternoon. His first game as United head coach is against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday.
Information from The Associated Press was used in this report.

items.text:
Tashima says Balogun red card row at World Cup prompted FIFA presidency bid
Tashima is one of three names on the ballot for the March election, along with current President Infantino and Diallo.
Japanese football official Kozo Tashima said on Friday that the handling of Folarin Balogun’s red card at the 2026 World Cup was what prompted him to run for FIFA president against Gianni Infantino.
FIFA suspended forward Balogun’s automatic one-match ban for a red card in July, allowing the American striker to play against Belgium after United States President Donald Trump said he had personally asked President Infantino to review the sanction.
The decision triggered a swift and fiery backlash and, along with an aborted attempt to sell a stake in FIFA tournaments, led to opposition to Infantino’s re-election as president.
Tashima said he wanted to restore trust in FIFA, drawing parallels with 2016, when Infantino took charge after a corruption scandal.
“Ten years ago something similar happened, and Mr Infantino became president to reform and improve things,” the Japan Football Association (JFA) honorary president told a news conference.
“He has certainly done wonderful things. But in this year, 2026, 10 years later, events have occurred that ignored governance.
“I have worked in football, especially as a player and coach. As such, I cannot accept Balogun’s red card in any way. On top of that, no explanation has been given even now. I felt very indignant about this, and that is why I decided to stand here.”
Following the Balogun incident, FIFA’s disciplinary committee said it had the authority to suspend the one-match ban, and that it operated independently.
FIFA last month said it would amend the rule in its disciplinary code, which had allowed for the reversal of the ban.
Working with Diallo
The election, set to be held in March next year, will be the first time since he won the post in 2016 that Infantino will face a challenge after being re-elected unopposed in 2019 and 2023.
French Football Federation President Philippe Diallo also announced a challenge on Monday with the backing of European governing body UEFA. Infantino has the support of Asia and Africa’s confederations.
“I have not actually received a nomination from any continental confederation. So I’m well aware that I’m at a considerable disadvantage in this race,” Tashima said.
“It’s a fact that Gianni’s support has been gradually declining. I will keep appealing to voters.”
Diallo said at a news conference on Tuesday that he would reach out to Tashima to “unite forces”. Tashima said he was open to the idea of coordinating with the Frenchman’s team to avoid splitting the anti-Infantino vote.
“I don’t think the French candidate’s entry puts me at a disadvantage. In fact, France has ties to Africa and other regions, so Mr Diallo’s entry may bring those votes,” he added.
“Watching his press conference, I saw that he pointed out FIFA’s accounting and other figures in great detail. I find it reassuring that such a professional has joined.”
‘Least conspicuous’ FIFA president
Tashima is a former Japan international and youth coach and the first Japanese candidate to stand for FIFA president. He has served on the FIFA Council since 2015.
The 68-year-old said that if elected, he would shun the spotlight.
“A foreign media person described me very accurately. They said that if I’m elected, I might become the least conspicuous president ever,” he said.
“That may have been a bit of irony, but I’m fine with it. It’s not the president who should stand out, but the players.”
He added that he would need to be modest in his campaigning, much of which would be funded by his own money.
“The JFA’s budget for this year is already set, so of course, I would like support from the JFA, but we’ll also have to gather funds, for example by creating a fund or running crowdfunding,” he said.
“I won’t spend wastefully. I also have no intention of flying by private jet or anything like that.”

In tennis, Arthur Fils was knocked out of the ATP Finals by Alexander Zverev (6-4, 7-6). Ben Shelton qualified for the semi-finals, while Carlos Alcaraz has been cleared to continue in the tournament following a reassuring MRI scan.

items.text:
Loneliness & mood swings - what's it like to miss a season through injury?
- Published
"I told my mother. I sat with her and I told her: 'Listen, I don't think I can play any more'," says Dejan Kulusevski in a moving interview about his injury nightmare.
It is 18 months since Tottenham and Sweden winger Kulusevski, 26, last started a competitive match.
Spurs have won the Europa League, sacked both Ange Postecoglou and Thomas Frank, "mutually agreed" to part ways with Igor Tudor and appointed Roberto de Zerbi since the former Juventus player last started a first-team game for his club.
A serious knee injury two weeks from the end of the 2024-25 season forced him to miss the whole of the following campaign, as well as the 2026 World Cup.
"You feel like the whole world has forgotten about you," adds Kulusevski in an interview with Tottenham's in-house media, external about the emotional toll of being out for so long.
Thankfully, the player nicknamed 'Deki' has made a full recovery and is closing in on his first Tottenham start since 11 May 2025.
He is not the only footballer to question their career after having their world turned upside down by injury.
In the women's game, Everton club captain Megan Finnigan recently returned from a cruciate ligament injury after 602 days out., external
"The amount of times the thought of retirement entered my head during rehab was a lot," Finnigan, 28, tells BBC Sport.
Countless hours in the gym away from team-mates, boredom, setbacks and frustration - what is it like for a player at the peak of their game to miss a season because of injury?
- 'I am a different man now' - Kulusevski on return after 526 days 
  - Published20 October
- Kulusevski out for a 'few months' - Postecoglou 
  - Published15 May 2025
'I stared at the wall for hours'
Before Crystal Palace visited Tottenham a fortnight from the end of the 2024-25 campaign, Kulusevski had much to look forward to.
Off the pitch, he was making plans to marry his partner Eldina Ahmic, a former midfielder with Swedish club Brommapojkarna and Bosnia-Herzegovina.
On the pitch, there was a Europa League final against Manchester United coming up.
Everything changed in that match against Palace.
In the early stages, Kulusevski stayed down after a challenge with Marc Guehi. He was able to climb to his feet and walk unaided off the pitch and straight down the tunnel.
But in that moment, his problems were only just starting.
"It was pain, but it didn't hurt that much," Kulusevski says, recalling the patella and cartilage injury in his right knee.
"I could feel that the knee was moving a little bit too much."
The initial diagnosis from Tottenham was that the £25m signing from Juventus, who arrived in the summer of 2023, would be out for "at least a few months".
Due to complications, those months turned into a year and Kulusevski's dream career threatened to turn into a nightmare.
He travelled to Bilbao on crutches to watch his team-mates beat United in the Europa League final.
"That was one of the hardest days of my life," he says. "It was so beautiful to see all the people happy, but for me I was going there with crutches, I couldn't work.
"I couldn't even go and get my medal because it was too slippy to go on that thing [platform].
"Seeing the team celebrating on the bus [outside Tottenham Hotspur Stadium] was probably one of the most difficult parts of this journey because you feel so alone.
"You feel like the whole world has forgot about you and what you put in."
As months went by, Kulusevski underwent multiple operations and was even offered a knee transplant as a treatment option, which he rejected.
"You get stressed because nothing works," he says.
Then came another crushing blow delivered in a phone call with Sweden boss Graham Potter. Stockholm-born Kulusevski, who had played for his country since the age of 19, would not be going to the 2026 World Cup.
He had hoped to recover in time to be selected.
"I just stared at the wall for three hours because I really believed I would do it," he says.
It is not just the players who suffer when they are out for so long; the people around them feel the emotional toll as well.
"Seeing him miss the Europa League final and the World Cup, every Premier League game last season, seeing him skipping around on his crutches, those parts were really difficult," Eldina, Kulusevski's wife, says.
As recently as this past summer, Kulusevski wondered whether he would play again.
"It had been one year and two months and I could still not walk up the stairs like a normal guy.
"I wasn't going to give up, but I also had to think if this didn't work out, what am I going to do, because I am 26 and I have to have some sort of plan."
Enormous comfort came from Leonie, Kulusevski's two-year-old daughter, during his bleakest days.
"I said if I cannot play football any more, I will still have fun with her."
Then, after multiple setbacks, came a crucial breakthrough.
His knee had healed sufficiently for specialists to give him permission to train again.
On 19 October, Kulusevski was given a hero's reception by Spurs fans when he made his first appearance in 526 days.
It came in Tottenham's 3-1 win over Coventry City as an 87th-minute substitute.
Waiting for him after the final whistle were Eldina and Leonie, his daughter wearing a Spurs shirt with the number 526 on the back, along with the words 'My Hero'.
He made his Sweden return this month, coming off the bench in a win against Bosnia-Herzegovina.
"Every day is just beautiful now," says Kulusevski, who has made four substitute appearances totalling 42 minutes for his club this season.
"I don't take it for granted any more."
'I wasn't pleasant to be around'
Research suggests female footballers are two to six times more likely to suffer anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injuries than their male counterparts.
Everton captain Finnigan remembers how she "completely lost my sparkle" as she endured the long road to recovery.

In a notice issued on Thursday, November
items.text:
NAIROBI, Kenya, Nov 20 – The National Police Service (NPS) has announced a nationwide recruitment exercise targeting Kenyans seeking to join the police service, with candidates expected to turn up at designated centres across the country on December 10, 2026.
In a notice issued on Thursday, November 19, the service invited suitably qualified Kenyans to apply for training as police constables, setting the recruitment exercise to run from 8am to 5pm.
The exercise will be conducted in 423 recruitment centres across the country, with applicants required to report to their respective centres by 8am.
According to the recruitment notice, applicants must be Kenyan citizens holding valid national identity cards and aged between 18 and 28 years.
Candidates must also have attained a minimum grade of D+ in the Kenya Certificate of Secondary Education (KCSE), with at least a D+ in either English or Kiswahili.
The service further requires applicants to be physically and medically fit, with minimum height requirements of 5 feet 8 inches for men and 5 feet 3 inches for women.
Applicants must also have no criminal record or pending criminal charges. Female candidates must not be pregnant at the time of recruitment or throughout the entire training period.
National Youth Service (NYS) graduates who meet the minimum entry requirements have also been encouraged to apply. Those applying through the NYS recruitment centre must present a discharge certificate indicating a minimum conduct rating of ‘GOOD’.
Interested candidates are required to download and complete the prescribed application forms available through the National Police Service, Kenya Police, Administration Police and Directorate of Criminal Investigations websites.
The forms can also be obtained from the nearest Huduma Centre.
Applicants will be required to present themselves at their respective recruitment centres with original documents and copies of their academic certificates and testimonials, national identity cards, birth certificates and NYS discharge certificates, where applicable.
In Nairobi, some of the designated recruitment venues include Moi Sports Centre Kasarani, Kamukunji Sports Grounds, Pumwani Playground, Dandora Stadium, City Stadium and Nyayo Stadium.
Other centres include Tena Grounds, Jakaranda Grounds, Vision Grounds in Makao Bora and Kenya Technical Training College grounds in Gigiri.
The police service has emphasised that the recruitment exercise is free and open to all eligible candidates, warning jobseekers against individuals demanding money in exchange for recruitment opportunities.
It cautioned that bribery, corruption and providing false or misleading information to influence the exercise constitute criminal offences punishable by law.
Members of the public have been urged to report suspected recruitment malpractices to the nearest police station or through the DCI’s toll-free hotline, 0800 722 203.
The recruitment comes as the National Police Service continues efforts to strengthen its workforce and enhance security operations across the country.
Successful candidates will undergo police training before being deployed to serve in the National Police Service.

items.summary:
US maritime agency warned Iran blockade was adding to rising Gulf premiums
US Maritime Administration acknowledged naval blockade's impact on insurance premiums and cargo capacity, memo shows.
The United States government’s maritime agency flagged the disruptive impact of Washington’s blockade of Ir
items.text:
US maritime agency warned Iran blockade was adding to rising Gulf premiums
US Maritime Administration acknowledged naval blockade's impact on insurance premiums and cargo capacity, memo shows.
The United States government’s maritime agency flagged the disruptive impact of Washington’s blockade of Iran on commercial shipping in an internal memo, documents obtained by Al Jazeera reveal.
In an alert, the US Maritime Administration (MARAD) acknowledged the Iran war’s negative impact on insurance premiums and cargo capacity after US Central Command (CENTCOM) announced that it had disabled a Panama-flagged bulk carrier for attempting to breach the blockade.
MARAD administrator Stephen M Carmel shared the alert with a subordinate on October 12, following CENTCOM’s attack on the vessel Ocean Molica and unattributed attacks on three other tankers in and around the Strait of Hormuz.
“Why it matters: This materially escalates the previous alert: merchant ships now face kinetic action from both sides, and the threat has spread to Gulf anchorages and the Gulf of Oman,” said the memo, titled “Alert – Hormuz risk expands beyond the strait”.
“That increases the likelihood of further war-risk premium spikes, crew refusals and effective tanker capacity contraction.”
Carmel shared the alert with MARAD colleague Michael Yarrington in an email requesting information about the impact of the attacks on insurance premiums and an update on the agency’s efforts to “rebuild” war risk insurance.
It is unclear whether the alert originated within MARAD or another agency.
“How is the insurance market responding to all this?” Carmel wrote to Yarrington, an official at MARAD’s Office of Marine Insurance.
Yarrington replied that a colleague had reached out to contacts in London for information and forwarded a summary of rising insurance premiums compiled from news reports.
Yarrington also shared a description of “core deliverables” considered crucial to MARAD’s work on war risk insurance, the details of which were redacted from the emails before their release.
Al Jazeera obtained the documents through a Freedom of Information Act request to MARAD, which is responsible for promoting the US maritime industry.
MARAD, which sits under the US Department of Transportation, the White House, the Department of Defence and CENTCOM, did not respond to requests for comment.
The emergence of the memo acknowledging the negative fallout of the blockade comes as a definitive end to the Iran war remains elusive after months of on-again, off-again negotiations between Washington and Tehran.
US President Donald Trump last week dismissed the need for a peace deal with Iran, days after suggesting that the conflict could end “fairly soon” and that renewed US strikes were “highly unlikely”.
“Those days have long since passed,” Trump wrote on Truth Social on Thursday. “We’ve got their money, Hundreds of Billions of Dollars, and we’ve got their Strait!”
Todd Huntley, a retired US Navy captain who leads the National Security Law Program at Georgetown University Law Center, said MARAD’s monitoring of the blockade was likely aimed at informing its advice to other branches of the US government.
“As far as I know, MARAD will issue general alerts on incidents or threats, but will not then discuss the consequences, eg, increases in insurance rates,” Huntley told Al Jazeera.
“I do think that some US officials either didn’t consider this risk or ignored it when ordering and implementing the blockade.
“To me, it was pretty obvious this was a likely development given past Iranian actions and threats.”
Ian Ralby, the CEO and founder of maritime security consultancy I.R. Consilium, said the Trump administration appeared to be less concerned about the “strategic considerations” of the blockade than preventing ships from contributing to Iran’s economic survival.
“The President has made it clear that he is unperturbed by the global economic fallout from the War – including the blockade – so it may also be the case that the potential consequences of the blockade were considered but dismissed as unimportant,” Ralby told Al Jazeera.
Global shipping has been roiled by attacks in the Strait of Hormuz and surrounding waters since the US and Israel launched strikes on Iran on February 28.
Some 130 attacks on vessels have been recorded in the region since the start of the conflict, resulting in the deaths of at least 25 seafarers, according to the International Maritime Organization (IMO).
October was the worst month for shipping since the war began, with 35 vessels targeted, according to the IMO.
While most attacks during the war have been blamed on Iran or Iranian-aligned forces, CENTCOM has claimed responsibility for destroying or disabling at least two dozen vessels, some of which it has identified as belonging to Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) shadow fleet.
The turmoil in the strait has sharply driven up costs for shipping lines.
The cost of insurance for an oil tanker carrying crude from the Middle East to East Asia surged about 200-fold from January to the end of October, reaching $12.29 per barrel, according to the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC).
As of July, insurers charged 3.5 percent–7.5 percent of a vessel’s market value for war risk cover, up from 0.10-0.25 percent before the war, according to industry estimates cited in the Parliament of Singapore, a major logistics and shipping hub.
Amid rising shipping costs, prices of crude oil and fertiliser have surged as much 60 percent and 112 percent, respectively, at various points during the war.
Boon Chuan Lim, an independent researcher in Singapore whose research on the turmoil in the Strait of Hormuz has been published in the Borsa Istanbul Review, said it was noteworthy that the Trump administration had placed enforcement of the blockade alongside other attacks when assessing disruption risk.

items.text:
LONDON, United Kingdom, Nov 20 — Up to 100,000 young people from the EU would be allowed to travel, work and study in the UK per year under a new youth mobility scheme set to be agreed on Friday, the BBC understands.
The same number of young Britons would be allowed into Europe under the scheme, expected to be approved at the UK-EU summit in Brussels. Downing Street has not commented on the details, but said talks were “down to the wire” on Thursday.
The prime minister has said a “Channel action plan” on immigration could also be struck, while negotiators are seeking agreements on food trade rules and carbon emissions pricing.
Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch has accused Andy Burnham of “reopening the divisions” of the Brexit referendum.
A new youth mobility scheme would aim to make it easier for young people to work and travel both in the EU and UK.
The UK already has schemes in place with 13 non-EU countries including Australia, Canada and India.
In 2024, the EU proposed allowing 18 to 30 year-olds to work or study in the EU and UK for up to four years.
Labour, which was then in opposition, rejected the deal – arguing it amounted to reinstating freedom of movement.
Since coming to government, the party has suggested it would consider a more restricted scheme with a time limit, a cap on the numbers coming to the UK and a ban on participants from claiming benefits.
The UK’s request to limit numbers has proved to be a sticking point in negotiation ahead of the summit, along with the EU’s request that EU students should pay the same tuition fees at UK universities as domestic students.
Speaking to broadcasters on Thursday evening, Burnham was asked if there were any circumstances in which the UK would walk away from a deal on Friday.
“There would always be those circumstances because I’m in this to get the best deal for Britain, always,” he said.
“But what’s in it for us is the possibility of lower food prices and I can’t turn my back on that, lower costs for business, cutting red tape, and a really big win potentially of more collaboration on immigration – a Channel action plan – which is a really big deal if we can land that tomorrow.
“So I hope people can understand why I have pushed this because it could be a really good deal for Britain.”
Burnham previously said the UK and EU could link up their law enforcement efforts, including sharing more data and criminal records of foreign nationals.
The prime minister’s spokesman has said if a deal were secured, the government would introduce legislation to Parliament next week to implement changes.
The Brexit debate is back – and there are nerves about what happens next
Faisal Islam: What’s in the Brexit reset food deal and are there trade-offs?
The EU that Burnham is eyeing up is very different to the one Britain left
An agreement on trade could remove checks and paperwork faced by food companies exporting to the EU.
The government argues this could add £5bn to the economy and cut food prices.
However, it could mean the UK will have to follow certain EU rules on products, for example on gene-edited crops or labelling.
Burnham has also said the summit would allow the UK to raise concerns about the Made in Europe scheme, which is designed to protect industries from unfair Chinese competition.
Burnham has previously suggested he could commit Labour to building a closer long-term future relationship with Europe, including asking to rejoin the organisation as a full member – however, he has ruled out major changes before the next election.
The party’s 2024 manifesto promised not to return to the EU, the single market, customs union or freedom of movement, which allows EU citizens to live and work elsewhere in the bloc without a visa.
Earlier this week, former deputy prime minister David Lammy urged the prime minister to go into the next general election promising to rejoin the EU.
However, the subject has divided his cabinet with one minister warning of the costs that would come with reversing Brexit.
Reform UK leader Nigel Farage, speaking to The Sun, said he does “not believe for a minute” the country would “ever vote to rejoin” the EU.
He added: “I think what Burnham is doing is playing a very cynical political game. He’s trying to pick up votes from the Lib Dems, pick up votes from the Greens, and using it as a massive distraction from all the problems that he can’t deal with.”
Speaking to the BBC’s Today programme on Thursday, Badenoch said she wanted to see easier trading with the EU, but “not trade at any cost”.
She also said the new deals could see UK companies having to follow EU rules, even those that do not trade with the bloc.
Liberal Democrat leader Sir Ed Davey told BBC Newsnight that while he agreed with Burnham on “the harms of Brexit”, he did not think the prime minister was “going to go anywhere near far enough”.
“We need to go further and faster,” he said, including returning to freedom of movement – which Sir Ed said would help tackle immigration and boost the UK economy.

items.title: The male footballers best associated with each shirt number – the readers’ edition
items.summary: Which footballers are inextricably linked to their shirt numbers? We picked out 50 players last week who have come to embody the numbers on their backs. It was not an exhaustive list – as our readers have proved. We couldn’t include some legends of the game – Pelé and Lionel Messi for a start – and
items.text:
Which footballers are inextricably linked to their shirt numbers? We picked out 50 players last week who have come to embody the numbers on their backs. It was not an exhaustive list – as our readers have proved. We couldn’t include some legends of the game – Pelé and Lionel Messi for a start – and we missed a few brilliant stories. Thankfully our readers have provided an alternative list. And, creative bunch that they are, they have begun with No 0 and ended with No 51 …
0
Hicham Zerouali
An honourable mention should go to Aberdeen’s No 0. Zerouali is one of the very few to have worn the number (before rules were changed in Scotland). He was a cult hero during a poor time at the club, who died tragically young in a car crash. Lewis
1
Bert Trautmann
The Manchester City No 1 in the 1940s, 1950s and 1960s. Your article said that Lev Yashin was an automatic choice for No 1. While mention was made of other goalkeepers, there was no nod in the direction of the great Bert Trautmann, the German prisoner of war who became a Manchester City legend. Yashin himself said “my only equal is the German boy at Manchester City”.
Bert’s goalkeeping achievements were many. He only started playing as a keeper in a prisoner of war team before signing for St Helens in the Lancashire Combination League on release from prison. A year later he signed for City, where he made more than 500 appearances as well as playing the last 17 minutes of the 1956 FA Cup final with a broken neck in the days before substitutes were allowed, making important saves towards the end to ensure a City victory. He was also the first goalkeeper voted Footballer of the Year.
Perhaps most remarkable of all, he saved 60% of penalties he faced. Unfortunately, he was not given any international recognition. As a German citizen he could not play for England and could only play for Germany if playing in the country. He would have been a certain starter in the Germany team that won the World Cup in 1954.
He also did as much as anyone to repair British-German relations after the second world war. He went from being booed by 20,000 people on his City debut to being feted by more than 50,000 fans at his 1964 testimonial. He was awarded an honorary OBE in 2004. David Cronin
3
Stuart Pearce
The greatest living Englishman; the best left-back to have played the game; the best player Nottingham Forest have ever had; and my hero (and Paolo Maldini’s). Will Kitchen
4
Billy Bremner
The captain who drove Leeds forwards for well over a decade. Captain of club and country, Bremner was the human personification of Don Revie’s team of the 1960s and 1970s. He had skill, drive, aggression, camaraderie and he played close to (and over?) the line. Thirty years after his early death, he is still the player who Leeds fans hold up as representing the qualities they value in players. It is fitting that the only player to come close to him while wearing the white No 4 was another diminutive, copper-haired Scotsman, Gordon Strachan. As the wee Scotsman with the statue outside Elland Road said: “Side before self, every time.” Nick Ramage
5
Billy Wright
Stan Cullis, the Wolves manager at the time, converted Wright from wing-half to centre-half. He was little more than 5ft 8in, which suggests he would not be a good fit in the position, but he could jump and time it right. He captained England and was the first footballer in the world to gain 100 caps. He also captained Wolves and led them to some headline victories, most notably against Honved. Most importantly of all: he represents football before 1960, when football was more open, more exciting and more rapid in the transition. Kevin R Cox
6
Bobby Moore
He was the greatest ever No 6. If Pelé described him as the best defender he ever played against, how can the Guardian not choose him? He excelled at timing, passing and the ability to read a game. He also inspired West Ham and England with his presence. Tim Evans
7
Stanley Matthews
There are still a few of us left who had the great pleasure to see the greatest No 7 of all time play, for Blackpool and Stoke City. His return to Stoke in the 1960s rejuvenated a team that had been stuck in the Second Division for a long time and helped put them back where they belonged, in the top flight. Matthews was the greatest No 7 of his day and, I would suggest, of all time. John Heath
9
Hughie Gallacher
I never saw him play but my father extolled his virtues to me. In this day and age when players are well paid, maybe overpaid, there should be a remembrance of those who went before them and created this wonderful game we call football. Nick Johnson
10
Pelé and Lionel Messi
So neither of the two greatest players to play the game, at least in my lifetime, is included. If we are talking about the beautiful game, then either Pelé (my preference) or Messi has to be the No 10. Richard Hirst
11
Mohamed Salah
Simply one of the best Premier League players this decade. His number 11 was often seen from behind, with the three defenders he was about to bamboozle looking worried in the background. Joe
15
Roberto Baggio
So obvious. Tom
16
Roy Keane
Keane was the most iconic and influential No 16. In the era of omnipresent Manchester United pundits, it’s easy to focus on the contemporary theatrical Keane playing the disgruntled, unimpressed one in the studio so well. But don’t lose sight of Keane winning duels, covering every blade of grass and spraying un-Hollywood but massively effective balls forward. Think Stadio delle Alpi, the scene where he tamed Zinedine Zidane and mounted a comeback against Juventus that enabled the Treble and all that. Think Lansdowne Road in 2001 when he essentially knocked out the Netherlands from the 2002 World Cup. Does Rodri have a movie with Steve Coogan in it? Michael Craig
18
Jürgen Klinsmann

items.title: England's All Blacks acid test, Erasmus circus, Boks to storm Dublin?
items.summary:
Nations Championship: England's All Blacks acid test at Twickenham, Rassie Erasmus circus, Springboks to storm to win vs Ireland in Dublin?
Third week of Nations Championship Tests in northern hemisphere sees England host the All Blacks in an acid test; Ireland welcome South Africa in bonkers week R
items.text:
Nations Championship: England's All Blacks acid test at Twickenham, Rassie Erasmus circus, Springboks to storm to win vs Ireland in Dublin?
Third week of Nations Championship Tests in northern hemisphere sees England host the All Blacks in an acid test; Ireland welcome South Africa in bonkers week Rassie Erasmus was handed six-Test ban; inaugural tournament concludes at Allianz Stadium Twickenham next weekend November 27-29
Thursday 19 November 2026 18:49, UK
The third weekend of Nations Championship Tests in the northern hemisphere is upon us, with England hosting the All Blacks in an acid test and Ireland facing the Springboks in the week a six-Test suspension was handed down to the controversial Rassie Erasmus...
England's All Blacks acid test
There is a sense of déjà vu, somewhat, for England this November when looking over their autumn performances and the general outlook emanating from them.
This time last year, England proved too strong for Australia and Fiji before welcoming New Zealand to Twickenham. In that Test, Steve Borthwick's side thrilled to a 33-19 victory over the All Blacks.
A nervy 27-23 win over Argentina followed, but England exited November buoyed by four wins, with many talking them up as a returning force in the world game, building towards Six Nations, Nations Championship and Rugby World Cup title tilts.
What followed was a disastrous Six Nations. The worst in England's history, in fact.
From five fixtures, they lost four for the first time ever, suffering defeat against Italy in a Test for the first time, as well as a record home loss to Ireland by a 42-21 margin at Twickenham.
They lost to Scotland for the fifth time in six years as the wheels well and truly came off a championship campaign which began with comfortable victory over a poor Wales side at home.
Displays in July's Nations Championship window were hardly overly positive either. A comprehensive 45-21 defeat in South Africa, a thrashing of a poor Fiji side in a Test bizarrely played in Liverpool, and holding on with 13 players to edge to victory in Argentina.
Borthwick and his players were suddenly under major pressure again, with stories of a camp rift emerging, but this month has seen 123 points scored in just two Tests - big victories over Australia and Japan.
Like last year, the All Blacks are coming to town with everyone wondering if England are back on track, or still a side short of the top table.
As such, Saturday's Test against a no-doubt angry New Zealand - following their shock defeat to Wales in Cardiff - represents something of an acid test for England.
Put on a show in victory, and talk of them as potentially one of the world's best will start to re-emerge. Suffer defeat, and criticism will filter back.
The circus of Rassie Erasmus
My word, it has been some week in Dublin as far as story-lines ahead of Saturday's crunch Ireland vs South Africa Test.
First, fly-half Sam Prendergast was cited for a hip-drop tackle committed against Fiji captain Peceli Yato in last week's 43-15 Ireland win - a first of its kind, with the manoeuvre outlawed at the start of this month.
Then, South Africa head coach Rassie Erasmus gave the mother and father of all press conferences. Even for him - and he has quite the history - it was downright bizarre.
Off the back of the Springboks losing to France in Paris last week - clearly the reason behind Erasmus' ticking demeanour - claims and comments from South Africa's revered rugby leader ranged from extraordinary to astonishing.
He began by predicting Prendergast would get off "on a technicality" and would play in Dublin on Saturday, claiming his double Rugby World Cup-winning squad and players were treated differently at disciplinary hearings than northern hemisphere players.
Erasmus even went so far as to state "things never seem to go our way." Make of that what you will when considering he is talking about a trophy-laden side who won the last World Cup following three successive one-point knockout victories.
Far worse was to follow when Erasmus claimed "17 knee-drop tackles" by France had been missed by the referee and TMO in South Africa's defeat last week - a figure almost universally debunked when reviewed by journalists and pundits in the aftermath.
Erasmus then came out with the claims which were likely the reasoning behind World Rugby snappily handing him a six-Test suspension: questioning whether TMO's and referees were "match-fixing" and whether there was "manipulation of the game or result" of Test matches.
When a journalist at the press conference commented to Erasmus he was making a "serious intimation", his response was: "It's not an accusation."
World Rugby didn't see it that way, and though South Africa Rugby requested a formal hearing take place, Erasmus has since taken to X to confirm he will watch Saturday's Test from his Dublin hotel room and has organised a free watchalong for anyone to sign up and view him and his reaction to the Test match as it is unfolding.
The 54-year-old has now been suspended three times in five years for these sorts of incidents, which constitute "public criticism of match officials, undermining the integrity of individuals or the sport, and fuelling online abuse."
Indeed, SA Rugby have since released a statement "condemning the online abuse of officials" following confirmation of Erasmus' ban.
During the 2021 British and Irish Lions series in South Africa, after the Springboks lost the first Test, Erasmus broadcasted an hour-long critique of Australian referee Nic Berry, and was eventually handed a two-month ban from all rugby activity and 10-month matchday ban.
Berry said afterwards Erasmus' behaviour had been an "assassination of my reputation" that caused "immeasurable damage." He no longer referees Tests involving South Africa.
World Rugby found the video had contained "multiple abusive and insulting comments and attacks on the officials."
In 2022 he received a two-Test ban after sarcastic social media posts

items.text:
Dillian Whyte offers to fight Deontay Wilder on December 11: ‘If Wilder wants it, they know where I am’
Dillian Whyte has made himself available to step in for Jai Opetaia and box Deontay Wilder on the undercard of the December 11 fight between Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff; "If they want it and they want to have a good fight, then I'm down," he said
Thursday 19 November 2026 18:07, UK
Dillian Whyte is ready to rekindle his rivalry with Deontay Wilder.
At one point Whyte was the WBC's No 1 contender when Wilder held that title. He never got to box Wilder, though did eventually challenge Tyson Fury after he'd beaten the American for the belt.
Wilder is currently looking for a new opponent after Jai Opetaia withdrew from a heavyweight bout that was scheduled for the undercard of Fury's December 11 showdown with Anthony Joshua.
Whyte has made himself available as a replacement. "If they want it then they know where I am," the Brixton heavyweight told Sky Sports News.
"If they want it and they want to have a good fight, then I'm down. You know, I always come to fight. I give it my best and I give my all.
"I've already waited 100 years for him, so if he wants it in December, then let's go."
He added: "I've been trying to fight him for 100 years. I've always believed that I could have beaten him.
"He's a big puncher, he's wiry, and he's fast and all that. I just believe that I have the mentality and the style to beat him and cause him all sorts of problems. And I still believe that."
Whyte insists he could be ready for the bill at the Principality Stadium. "I'm training to fight a week after them. So I'm in a gym, I'm looking to come back December 18. So if they want it, I'm here.
"All have to do is let me know."

items.title: US welcomes American consortium’s selection for Mrima Hill mining project
items.summary:
NAIROBI, Kenya, Nov 20 — The United States has welcomed Kenya’s selection of a US-led consortium to develop the Mrima Hill rare earths and niobium project in Kwale County, describing the decision as a commitment to transparency and economic cooperation.
The US State Department’s Bureau of African Af
items.text:
NAIROBI, Kenya, Nov 20 — The United States has welcomed Kenya’s selection of a US-led consortium to develop the Mrima Hill rare earths and niobium project in Kwale County, describing the decision as a commitment to transparency and economic cooperation.
The US State Department’s Bureau of African Affairs congratulated Frontier Minerals Consortium on its selection, saying the choice of an American consortium would bring innovation, local value addition and economic opportunities to Kenya.
“Congratulations to Frontier Minerals for being selected to develop the Mrima Hill rare earths and niobium project in Kenya,” the bureau said in a statement on Thursday.
“The choice of an American consortium reflects a commitment from the Kenyan government to develop their mining sector in a transparent manner that will bring market-leading innovation to Kenya, ensure local value addition, and create jobs and economic benefits for [the United States and Kenya].”
The endorsement follows Kenya’s announcement of successful bidders for three strategic mineral projects after a competitive tender process and statutory procurement reviews.
The Ministry of Mining, Blue Economy and Maritime Affairs named Frontier Minerals Consortium as the preferred bidder for the Mrima Hill project, which targets niobium, rare earth elements and other minerals.
The consortium comprises Frontier Minerals LLC, Bunker Hill Mining Corp, ReElement Technologies and American Resources Corporation.
A joint venture between China’s Fangda Special Steel Technology Co. Ltd and Sinohydro Corporation was selected for the Kang’ura Chromite Development Project in Samburu County and the Kamacabi Copper Development Project in Tharaka Nithi County.
The government said no responsive qualifying bids were received for the Lali Hills Manganese Project in Tana River County and the Kiritiri Coltan Project in Embu County, which will be addressed separately in accordance with the law.
Licensing process still pending
The Ministry clarified that the notices issued to successful bidders were Notices of Intention to Award and did not amount to mining or prospecting licences.
The selected bidders must first engage host communities, landowners, county leadership and other relevant stakeholders, and obtain the necessary consents under the Mining Act.
They are also required to submit prospecting licence applications through the Ministry’s Online Mining Cadastre portal, accompanied by the required consents, statutory documents and fees.
The applications will then be submitted to the Mineral Rights Board for independent statutory scrutiny and recommendations before the Cabinet Secretary can grant licences.
Cabinet Secretary Hassan Ali Joho said the tender outcome should not be mistaken for immediate authorisation to begin exploration.
“An award at the end of a tender process is not a licence to immediately break ground; rather, it is the gateway to meaningful local partnership and strict regulatory compliance,” Joho said.
He said host communities should be informed about the companies seeking to operate in their areas, their technical capabilities and financial capacity, as well as their commitments to environmental protection, cultural heritage, local employment and community development.
The Ministry said the tender evaluation considered bidders’ geological and exploration expertise, plans for in-country mineral processing and beneficiation, local content, environmental restoration and financial capacity.
Successful bidders were required to attain a minimum technical score of 80 per cent before proceeding to financial evaluation.
